title: Initial load shows a spinner on a black screen — no poster/backdrop art
symptom: After pressing play on a movie/episode/channel, the customer sees a black screen with a small centered indeterminate spinner for the entire cold-start window (typically 2-5s on a Fire Stick, longer on weak wifi). It reads as 'the app froze / the stream is broken', not 'content is loading'.
trigger: Every press-play (VOD, Series, Live) and every Live channel zap. The Leanback VideoSupportFragment SurfaceView is black until onRenderedFirstFrame, and the only feedback is the bare ProgressBar.
rootCause: showBufferingOverlay() (2151-2169) builds ONLY a bare indeterminate ProgressBar centered via Gravity.CENTER and adds it over the transparent fragment (view background is TRANSPARENT, line 202/207) atop a black SurfaceView. The class extends VideoSupportFragment (line 81) whose SurfaceView stays black until the first decoded frame. streamIcon IS passed to newInstance and stored in viewModel.streamIcon (3401-3425, onCreate 3435) but is never rendered as a backdrop behind the spinner. onRenderedFirstFrame (ExoPlayerDiagnosticListener:70) only logs — there is no first-frame-driven crossfade because there is no art to cross-fade. Confirmed: zero backdrop/poster ImageView in the player view hierarchy.
fix: Add a full-screen ImageView behind the SurfaceView; the instant onViewCreated runs (before prepare()) load viewModel.streamIcon (VOD/Series poster, or channel logo + neutral gradient for Live) via Coil with a subtle dim scrim, keep the spinner on top, and crossfade it out (~200ms) when onRenderedFirstFrame fires. The card art is already in Coil's memory cache from the row the user just clicked, so this is near-free. Makes the same TTFF feel intentional/branded instead of broken.
benchmark: Netflix/Disney+/Prime/Hulu always paint the title's key art/backdrop (often with logo + shimmer) during spin-up and only swap to video on first frame — the customer never sees a lone spinner on black. This applies fully to IPTV (it's a UX layer, independent of single-bitrate streaming).
correction: Confirmed exactly as reported. P1 is the correct severity — this is perceptual, not a TTFF regression; the start itself isn't broken, it just looks broken. The biggest single perceived-quality win in this dimension.

title: [MISSED] On cold start the spinner is hidden on STATE_READY, before the first frame paints — a beat of pure black with no spinner
symptom: On the initial start, right at the end of buffering, the customer can see the spinner vanish a fraction of a second BEFORE any picture appears — leaving a brief window of totally black screen with no spinner at all (looks even more like a freeze/crash than the spinner did).
trigger: Every cold start (VOD/Series/Live). Worse on slow decoders (mt8695/mt8167) where decoder init after STATE_READY adds latency before onRenderedFirstFrame.
rootCause: showBufferingOverlay(false) is called on Player.STATE_READY (line 1152). STATE_READY means 'enough buffered to start', which fires before onRenderedFirstFrame (decoder still spinning up the first output buffer). Nothing keys the overlay-hide off the actual first frame, so on slow decoders the spinner disappears while the SurfaceView is still black. Compounds black-screen-no-poster — without a backdrop, this is a black-on-black gap.
fix: Keep the buffering overlay (and the proposed backdrop) visible until onRenderedFirstFrame, not until STATE_READY. Wire the diagnostic listener's onRenderedFirstFrame (or add a video AnalyticsListener) to hide/crossfade the overlay. Cheap and removes the worst-feeling micro-window.
benchmark: Top platforms only reveal video and dismiss loading art on first decoded frame, never on the 'ready to start' signal — so there is never a black gap between spinner-gone and picture-shown.
correction: [MISSED] The auditor's black-screen finding stops at 'spinner on black'. The real code is slightly worse: the spinner is dismissed on STATE_READY (1152), not on first frame, so there's a brief spinner-less black gap on slow Fire Stick decoders. Fixing finding #1 plus this together is the correct scope.

title: No stream pre-warm / preconnect — press-play pays the cold-connection handshake
symptom: First-frame is slower than necessary on the first play of a session and on channel zaps because DNS→TCP→TLS→302→first-segment happens cold at click time.
trigger: First play of a session; each Live channel zap (tuneToChannel re-resolves a possibly-new CDN host).
rootCause: Both pre-warm paths warm METADATA only: PredictivePreFetcher.prefetchIfNeeded fetches EPG for top channels (43-50); preWarmSection warms category lists (213-223). Neither preconnects to the stream-byte host nor pre-buffers media. So setMediaItem()+prepare() (420-428 / zap 2632-2635) starts cold. The stream DataSource reuses the shared OkHttp client/pool (StreamingDataFactories:62-65) — which only helps when a connection to that exact host:port was opened recently.
fix: Cheap win: on poster/channel focus dwell (reuse ScreenPreWarmer's 500ms debounce) issue an OkHttp preconnect (HEAD or 1-byte ranged GET) to the resolved stream host so DNS+TCP+TLS+302 are warm at click. The adjacent-channel media pre-buffer (second ExoPlayer / Media3 preload) should be MID/HIGH-tier only — it is unsafe on the 1GB-RAM primary target and would compete with the existing LivePreviewManager. Preconnect alone is near-free and the right 80/20.
benchmark: Netflix/YouTube TV preconnect and pre-buffer the likely-next title on hover; YouTube TV pre-tunes adjacent channels. Valid as a UX/network technique even for single-bitrate IPTV — but the realistic win is the handshake (typically a few hundred ms, occasionally ~1s on slow DNS), NOT 'a noticeable second or more' on every play as the auditor implies.
correction: Confirmed: no stream-host preconnect, prewarm is metadata-only. But the auditor OVER-states magnitude and severity. (1) In many Xtream setups the stream-byte host == the API host (flarecoral.com), which Retrofit already keeps warm in the shared pool — so the cold tax only fully applies when the provider 302-redirects to a separate CDN. (2) The preconnect saves the handshake (hundreds of ms), not the dominant first-segment-download time. (3) The 'pre-buffer adjacent channels' half is risky on 1GB RAM and the auditor under-weights that. Net: real but P2, not P1, and the preconnect (not the pre-buffer) is the part worth doing.

title: VOD/Series resume re-reads the DB on the press-play critical path (position already known one screen earlier)
symptom: On a partially-watched movie/episode there's a tiny extra delay before the player even starts connecting, because the resume position is read from Room before setMediaItem/prepare — and the same value was already queried one screen earlier to drive the resume dialog.
trigger: Pressing play on any Continue Watching item (highest-intent content).
rootCause: needsResume (411) launches a coroutine that awaits getResumePositionSync() (418, a Room read in PlayerViewModel:77-83) before setMediaItem(uri, pos)+prepare()+play(). HomeFragment.playVodWithResumeCheck already queried getWatchProgress(streamId) (1871) to decide the resume dialog, but only forceStartFromBeginning (a boolean) is passed into newInstance (1881-1888) — the resolved position is dropped, so the player re-reads the DB on the latency path.
fix: Pass the resolved resume position from playVodWithResumeCheck into newInstance as a long arg; in onCreate/onViewCreated call setMediaItem(uri, resumeArg); prepare(); play() synchronously with no coroutine and no second Room read. Fall back to the async query only for deep-link entry where the position wasn't pre-resolved.
benchmark: Netflix/Prime resolve the bookmark from title metadata they already hold and hand it to the player as a parameter — no DB hop in the press-play→first-frame window.
correction: Code confirmed exactly (redundant read, position not threaded through newInstance). But P2 is inflated to P3: a Room point-read on an indexed single row is ~1-5ms and runs on Dispatchers.IO; it is swamped by network TTFF (hundreds of ms to seconds). It's a real, easy cleanup but the customer does not perceptibly feel it. P3 polish, not P2 friction. The setMediaItem(item, positionMs) resume design itself is correct (no watch-the-logo-then-jump).

title: Buffering spinner has no debounce — flashes on sub-second mid-movie rebuffers
symptom: Tiny transient rebuffers and ExoPlayer's BUFFERING→READY cycling (format changes, segment boundaries on poorly-muxed IPTV TS) flash the spinner for a fraction of a second over the held last frame, reading as a momentary blink rather than smooth playback.
trigger: Brief network dips, TS segment boundaries, and the rapid BUFFERING→READY cycling the code itself tracks as a 'buffer storm' (1131-1149).
rootCause: STATE_BUFFERING immediately calls showBufferingOverlay(true) (1129) and STATE_READY immediately hides it (1152) with no minimum-visible / delayed-show debounce. A 200ms rebuffer paints a 200ms spinner flash over the held frame.
fix: Debounce: on STATE_BUFFERING post a ~350ms delayed show; on STATE_READY cancel the pending show and hide. Short rebuffers that recover inside the window never paint a spinner. Keep the cold-start spinner immediate (covered by the proposed backdrop). Must NOT debounce the initial start indicator and must not interfere with the frame watchdog's explicit showBufferingOverlay(true) (1577-1580).
benchmark: Top platforms hold the last frame and only reveal a buffering indicator after a perceptibility threshold (a few hundred ms), so brief dips recover invisibly.
correction: Confirmed: no debounce; immediate show on BUFFERING, immediate hide on READY. P3 is correct — mid-movie the SurfaceView holds the last frame so it's a spinner-over-frame blink, not breakage, and the stall detector/frame watchdog handle real hangs. Pure polish. Implementer caveat: don't let the debounce swallow the watchdog's own deliberate overlay-show at 1577-1580.

title: Sustained-stall recovery does a hard player.stop() that black-screens the SurfaceView instead of holding the last frame
symptom: On a stall that outlasts the timeout, the picture goes fully BLACK with a bare spinner for the retry delay (1s first attempt, escalating 3/5/8/12/15s), then the stream cold-restarts from an empty buffer — a black void rather than a brief pause-and-resume.
trigger: LIVE stays in STATE_BUFFERING for the FULL 15s (or VOD/SERIES 30s) — e.g. a 15-20s WiFi sag. NOT every dip: a dip shorter than the timeout auto-resumes from STATE_BUFFERING with no stop().
rootCause: startStallDetector() (line 1492) waits delay(stallTimeout) = 15s LIVE / 30s VOD, then if STILL STATE_BUFFERING calls p.stop() (line 1505) which clears the decoder output. Video renders onto Leanback's raw SurfaceView via LeanbackPlayerAdapter (line 383) with the fragment background forced TRANSPARENT (202/207) — when the decoder stops the surface shows through to black. There is no shutter image and no setKeepContentOnPlayerReset because that is a Media3 PlayerView API and this app uses VideoSupportFragment, not PlayerView. So the recovery is felt as a black screen, not a held frame.
fix: Don't p.stop() on the first 1-2 LIVE/VOD stall escalations — leave the player in STATE_BUFFERING so it refills and resumes from whatever buffer remains (invisible recovery; ExoPlayer auto-resumes with no stop). Only escalate to stop()/prepare() after a longer threshold when the source is genuinely dead. Additionally hold the last frame: capture the last rendered bitmap into an ImageView shown over the SurfaceView during any stop/rebuild, or move the video surface to a Media3 PlayerView with setKeepContentOnPlayerReset(true)+setShutterBackgroundColor.
benchmark: Netflix/YouTube TV freeze on the last rendered frame, show a subtle inline spinner only after a grace period, refill in the background, and resume without ever clearing to black or cold-restarting the stream.
correction: Severity corrected P0->P1. The auditor's framing has two holes: (1) the hard stop() does NOT fire on transient dips — it only fires after the FULL 15s LIVE / 30s VOD timeout while STILL STATE_BUFFERING (guard at line 1499); dips shorter than that auto-resume natively with no stop and no black screen. The triage rules in CLAUDE.md note that real-world 13-15s sustained refills are customer-side-network-bound, where SOME interruption is unavoidable. (2) The 'fires on every watchdog frozen-frame escalation' claim is WRONG — watchdog step 1 is a 50ms seek-flush (seekToDefaultPosition), not stop(); stop() only appears in the harder rebuild rungs (e.g. line 1655) which are decoder-fallback cases, not transient-network cases. The genuine, real gap is correct: the recovery that DOES fire produces a felt black void + no last-frame hold + a bare spinner. That is a quality hiccup (P1), not a 'frequently breaks watching' P0, because it is gated to sustained stalls that are mostly genuine network failures.

title: Buffering spinner pops instantly on every STATE_BUFFERING with no debounce, no scrim, and no minimum-show time
symptom: A bare, unstyled gray indeterminate ProgressBar blinks onto the screen for even sub-second rebuffers and strobes on/off during a buffer storm (BUFFERING->READY->BUFFERING). Makes the app look like it is struggling even when recovery is instant.
trigger: Any momentary buffer underrun: a brief WiFi blip on live TV, the first-frame buffer of every channel zap, a format/track change, or rapid BUFFERING/READY cycling on a marginal connection.
rootCause: onPlaybackStateChanged STATE_BUFFERING calls showBufferingOverlay(true) synchronously with zero delay (line 1129); STATE_READY hides it immediately (line 1152). showBufferingOverlay (2151-2169) lazily creates a default android.widget.ProgressBar (indeterminate, WRAP_CONTENT, centered) with no scrim, no theme, no debounce timer and no minimum-visible floor, then just toggles visibility. Short rebuffers therefore flash; storms strobe.
fix: Debounce: on STATE_BUFFERING, post showBufferingOverlay(true) with ~700-1000ms delay and cancel it if STATE_READY arrives first, so sub-second rebuffers are invisible. Once shown, enforce a ~500ms minimum on-screen time to stop strobing. Replace the raw ProgressBar with a styled, scrim-backed indicator matching the cinematic theme.
benchmark: Top platforms suppress short rebuffers entirely and only reveal a spinner once a stall crosses ~1s, then keep it stable — the customer never sees a strobing or instantly-flashing indicator.
correction: Confirmed exactly as described. The v3.6.4 release notes do explicitly defer this 'cycling spinner' fix, and buffer-storm detection (BUFFER_STORM_THRESHOLD=5 over 30s, line 1138) only triggers an FFmpeg rebuild on HEVC — it does NOT suppress the spinner. One addition worth noting: the watchdog also fires a Toast 'Optimizing video playback...' (line 1581-1583) alongside this spinner on frozen-frame paths, compounding the same 'app is struggling' impression. Severity P1 is correct (felt-quality, not a watch-breaker).

title: Pre-buffer is sized once at player creation and never adapts; on the primary 1GB stick it is a fixed thin 3s/8s LIVE buffer
symptom: On a good-but-jittery connection the app keeps a thin pre-buffer (LIVE 3s min / 8s max on the 1GB Fire Stick) and rebuffers on dips it could have ridden out; on a degrading pipe it never deepens the buffer pre-emptively, so the customer hits repeated buffer->drain->rebuffer cycles instead of one deep refill.
trigger: Any session on the primary target (1GB Fire Stick, memoryClass<=192 -> forLowMemory: LIVE 3s/8s, VOD 10s/30s) with intermittent jitter.
rootCause: The DefaultLoadControl is built once (line 226-230) and DefaultLoadControl can't be resized at runtime, so the pre-buffer is static for the whole session. On the PRIMARY 1GB target the gate at line 226 (memoryClass<=192) sends it to BufferConfigs.forLowMemory = fixed LIVE 3s/8s — QualityPolicy.tier is BYPASSED there. Only on devices with memoryClass>192 does the buffer come from forContentTypeAndQuality(tier), and that tier (QualityPolicy.kt:24) is derived from NetworkCapabilities.linkDownstreamBandwidthKbps (NetworkMonitor.kt:67), the static, frequently-wrong OS link hint that defaults to MEDIUM. The real per-stream throughput from DefaultBandwidthMeter is read only for diagnostic logging in PlaybackHealthMonitor (line 74) and never fed back to size buffers.
fix: Two separable levers. (a) Raise the LIVE minBuffer floor in forLowMemory from 3s to ~6s within the 1GB memory budget so a single short dip doesn't drain to empty (most impactful for the primary device). (b) For higher-memory tiers, drive QualityPolicy from DefaultBandwidthMeter.bitrateEstimate (already measured) rather than the OS link hint, and grow the target buffer on sustained low headroom by recreating the player's load control — pre-buffer through jitter the way ABR-less players must.
benchmark: Netflix/YouTube TV continuously measure real segment throughput and keep a buffer sized to ride out jitter, proactively deepening it as the pipe degrades — never relying on a static OS link hint.
correction: Severity corrected P1->P2 and the root cause is PARTIALLY MIS-ROOTED. The auditor pinned this on 'sized from a near-useless OS bandwidth estimate', but on the PRIMARY 1GB Fire Stick (memoryClass<=192) QualityPolicy.tier is BYPASSED — the buffer is the fixed forLowMemory 3s/8s config, so the bad-tier-signal critique applies only to memoryClass>192 devices, NOT the primary target the summary leads with. The thin-buffer symptom on the 1GB stick is real (via forLowMemory), the static/non-adaptive critique is real, but per the CLAUDE.md triage rules the dominant real-world cause of 13-15s refills is customer-side sustained-throughput collapse that a deeper pre-buffer only PARTIALLY masks (and cannot fix) on single-bitrate IPTV. A bigger buffer raises start latency and memory on a 1GB device, so the win is bounded — P2, not P1. The 'Netflix continuously measures throughput' benchmark only partly applies: Netflix's main lever is ABR rung-switching, which single-bitrate IPTV does not have; only the pre-buffer-depth sub-claim transfers.

title: Live channel zap clears to a spinner with no last-frame hold, making every channel change feel like a rebuffer
symptom: Changing channels makes the previous picture vanish to black + bare spinner for the new stream's first-frame buffer, instead of a clean cut or held frame. With the thin LIVE buffer the zap can feel sluggish and indistinguishable from a mid-stream rebuffer.
trigger: Every live channel change via tuneToChannel (D-pad zap / channel list select).
rootCause: tuneToChannel does player.setMediaItem(newUri) -> prepare() -> play() (lines 2633-2635) on the existing player. While the new source buffers, STATE_BUFFERING fires and the same scrim-less spinner (showBufferingOverlay) appears over a SurfaceView whose previous output was flushed by setMediaItem. There is no last-frame hold during the source swap and no per-channel prefetch.
fix: Hold the last frame of the outgoing channel (captured bitmap over the surface, or a PlayerView shutter) until onRenderedFirstFrame of the new channel, and suppress the spinner for the first ~700ms of the zap (shared with the micro-rebuffer debounce fix). Optionally pre-warm the next/prev channel's first segments to push zap time under 1.5s.
benchmark: YouTube TV / cable-style apps target <1.5s channel change presented as a clean cut or held frame, never a black void with a generic spinner.
correction: Confirmed as written. Existing mitigations the auditor credited are accurate: mute-before-load (line 2631/2636) avoids the audio pop, LIVE minPlaybackMs=500 (BufferConfigs:15) speeds time-to-picture, and the channel banner is posted after delay(500) (line 2649-2651). None of them holds the outgoing frame, so the black+spinner flash on each zap is real. P2 is correct — this is friction, not a watch-breaker, and the fix is the SAME last-frame-hold + spinner-debounce mechanism as the P0/P1 above, so it should be bundled.

title: Every channel change flashes a black screen behind a bare centered spinner
symptom: On each DPAD_UP/DOWN channel change the video area cuts to a full black SurfaceView with only a small centered indeterminate ProgressBar — no held last frame, no channel-branded backdrop, no progress sliver. Reads as 'the TV blinked off' between channels. Worst on slow pipes / ULTRA_LOW sticks where buffer fill takes longer, but the connect+first-frame black window is visible even on fast wifi.
trigger: Any live-TV channel up/down zap (D-pad, controls-bar prev/next, or horizontal fling on phone), every single press, the moment tuneToChannel commits.
rootCause: tuneToChannel() (line 2631 mute, 2633-2635 setMediaItem/prepare/play) reuses the same ExoPlayer attached to a Leanback VideoSupportFragment SurfaceView (class declared line 81 `: VideoSupportFragment()`). ExoPlayer tears down the prior decoder output on prepare(), so the SurfaceView renders black until the new stream's first frame. STATE_BUFFERING (line 1128) calls showBufferingOverlay(true), which only adds a bare WRAP_CONTENT centered ProgressBar over black (lines 2154-2163) — no scrim, no backdrop, no channel info. Grep-confirmed: setKeepContentOnPlayerReset and setShutterBackgroundColor appear NOWHERE in app/src/main (zero hits) — and a raw Leanback SurfaceView has no PlayerView shutter to set anyway. Fragment background is transparent (lines 202/207) so there is no masking layer; onRenderedFirstFrame is not handled to fade anything.
fix: Add a video-area mask that appears instantly on zap and fades on first frame: a full-screen dark scrim (#CC0A0A0A) carrying the target channel logo+name+number and a thin indeterminate bar, shown synchronously when tuneToChannel starts, dismissed on the first rendered frame (register an AnalyticsListener.onRenderedFirstFrame, currently unused, to drive the fade). Show the channel-info immediately rather than via the existing 500ms-delayed banner (lines 2649-2652). Optionally hold the prior SurfaceView/TextureView frame as a freeze-bitmap under the scrim so the change crossfades instead of cutting to black, and defer the spinner ~400ms so sub-400ms zaps show no spinner.
benchmark: YouTube TV and cable-style guides crossfade or show a channel-branded loading card (logo + progress sliver) and never expose a black surface; Netflix holds a backdrop/box-art during any source switch. The single-bitrate-IPTV caveat does not apply here — this is purely a perceived-transition / shutter-masking gap, not an ABR claim, so the benchmark is fair.
correction: Confirmed real and correctly P1. Two precision corrections to the auditor's framing (neither changes severity): (1) The black does NOT span 'the full 300ms debounce + connect + buffer'. During the 300ms debounce window the OLD frame stays on screen — the player is untouched until the debounced tuneToChannel fires (debouncedTune lines 2361-2367). Black starts at setMediaItem (2633), so the gap is connect+first-frame only (~1.5-3s typical), not debounce-inclusive. (2) The auditor's cited line 2593 is the tuneToChannel signature; the actual mute+setMediaItem+prepare+play is lines 2630-2636. LoadControl fast-first-frame tuning is real (BufferConfigs LIVE: setBufferDurationsMs(5000,15000,500,1500)+setPrioritizeTimeOverSizeThresholds(true), line 14-16) but only speeds the gap, doesn't mask it. Gap stands.

title: Preview→fullscreen re-buffers the SAME stream from scratch instead of handing off the warm player
symptom: After the side-panel live preview has been playing, pressing OK to go fullscreen makes the picture disappear and re-buffer (spinner + black, ~1.5-3s) before the identical channel returns — the customer waits a second time for content they were already watching.
trigger: Live TV screen on a MID/HIGH Fire Stick: focus a channel, wait ~1s for auto-preview to start, then press OK. (Does NOT occur if OK is pressed within ~1s of focus — no preview ran yet — nor on ULTRA_LOW/<=128MB sticks where auto-preview is gated off entirely.)
rootCause: goFullscreen() (line 830) calls stopPreview()→previewManager.release() (LivePreviewManager 84-89: stop/clearVideoSurface/release the warm ExoPlayer that already buffered the stream), then `tx.replace` launches a brand-new OoustreamPlaybackFragment (844-854) that constructs a fresh ExoPlayer and cold-starts the identical URL via tuneToChannel/setMediaItem. The buffered media, open socket, and warm decoder are discarded; the fullscreen player starts from zero, re-paying the first-frame cost (compounded by the black-gap-on-zap shutter gap, finding #1).
fix: Either hand the preview's warm ExoPlayer to the fullscreen surface (single-engine Media3 makes this feasible: clearVideoSurface on the preview PlayerView, reattach the SAME player to the fullscreen Leanback SurfaceView — no stop/release), OR at minimum capture the preview's last frame as a freeze-frame backdrop behind the fullscreen spinner so the cold start has no visible black gap. The latter is the cheaper, lower-risk fix and dovetails with finding #1's shutter mask.
benchmark: YouTube / Prime Video hover-previews expand the SAME already-playing stream to fullscreen with a scale/crossfade, no re-buffer. This benchmark applies (it's about not discarding a warm pipe, independent of ABR).
correction: Confirmed real, but DOWNGRADED P1→P2. The auditor's 'any preview→fullscreen entry' overstates scope two ways verified in code: (a) auto-preview only fires after a ~1s focus dwell (LiveTvFragment 378-387) AND is gated TV-only AND off on lowMemoryDevice (memoryClass<=128, line 112) — so on the ULTRA_LOW sticks the auditor flags as 'worst,' NO preview ever runs and there is no double-wait (just one normal cold start). (b) A quick OK (within the dwell) also incurs no preview, so no double-wait. The double cold-start is real ONLY on MID/HIGH sticks where the user dwelled long enough for preview to start — a real but narrower window, and the second start lands on the same fast LIVE LoadControl. Customer-felt cost is one extra ~1.5-3s re-buffer in that specific path, not a watch-breaking interruption → P2 friction, not P1.

title: Every recovery path goes to BLACK + spinner instead of freezing the last frame
symptom: Mid-movie, on any rebuffer or decoder recovery, the picture vanishes to a black screen with a small centered indeterminate spinner (and on SW/FFmpeg-video rebuilds, a 'Optimizing video decoder...' / 'Optimizing video playback…' toast) for the full recovery duration, then video pops back. It reads as 'the stream broke,' not 'a momentary dip.'
trigger: A transient network dip (STATE_BUFFERING at line 1128-1130), a network disconnect/reconnect (line 1377-1379 also shows a bare spinner), the stall detector firing (p.stop() at 1505), OR any of the three player rebuilds (rebuildPlayerWithSoftwareDecoder 1835, rebuildPlayerWithFfmpegVideoDecoder 1955, rebuildPlayerWithFfmpegPreferred 2048). Hits hardest on the 1GB Fire TV Sticks that need rebuilds most.
rootCause: The fragment extends Leanback VideoSupportFragment (line 81), whose video surface is a SurfaceView. showBufferingOverlay() (2151-2169) just adds a WRAP_CONTENT indeterminate ProgressBar gravity-centered over that SurfaceView — there is no captured bitmap of the last frame painted under it. On the stall path the detector calls p.stop() (1505); every rebuild calls safeReleasePlayer() (1404-1410) which does p.clearVideoSurface() + p.release() then builds a fresh ExoPlayer re-attached via a new LeanbackPlayerAdapter. The instant the producing decoder's output stops or the surface is cleared, a SurfaceView is black — nothing keeps painting the last frame. There is no setKeepContentOnPlayerReset / TextureView snapshot / artwork anywhere in the player package (verified by grep). The 'Optimizing video decoder...' Toast (1934) on the SW rebuild and 'Optimizing video playback…' Toast (1582) on the watchdog are literal during-black UX.
fix: Hold the last frame across recovery. Cleanest given the SurfaceView base: before stop()/clearVideoSurface(), capture the current frame (the simplest reliable route is to render video to a TextureView via the player's setVideoTextureView and snapshot getBitmap() into an ImageView placed above the surface, OR migrate the surface to PlayerView with setKeepContentOnPlayerReset(true)). Show that frozen frame (optionally with a small corner spinner, not a centered spinner on black) during recovery and cross-fade to live on the new player's onRenderedFirstFrame. Drop the two 'Optimizing…' Toasts (1582, 1934) — recovery should be silent.
benchmark: Netflix/YouTube TV freeze the last decoded frame and refill the buffer (or swap decoder) underneath it; the viewer sees a steady picture, at most a tiny spinner, never a black screen for a sub-few-second dip. This benchmark DOES apply to single-bitrate IPTV — hold-last-frame is a presentation technique independent of ABR.
correction: Confirmed against the actual code. The base class is VideoSupportFragment (SurfaceView), showBufferingOverlay is a bare centered ProgressBar, safeReleasePlayer does clearVideoSurface()+release(), and no last-frame-retention mechanism exists anywhere in player/. The auditor's PlayerView.setKeepContentOnPlayerReset suggestion is slightly off — this isn't a PlayerView, it's Leanback's SurfaceView, so that exact API isn't wired; the TextureView-snapshot route is the applicable fix. Severity P1 is correct: it is genuinely felt on every recovery and on the exact 1GB devices that recover most, but it does not break/stop watching, so it is not a P0. The existing spinner mitigation is real but does not address the black-screen feeling, so alreadyHandled=false.

title: Buffering spinner flashes on every sub-second transient and on every channel change
symptom: A spinner blinks on/off on a slightly-unstable connection and flashes for a fraction of a second on every channel zap and on every brief network blip — visual noise that makes a basically-fine stream look unstable.
trigger: Any STATE_BUFFERING transition, including the routine BUFFERING→READY churn ExoPlayer does, the brief buffering at the start of every channel zap (tuneToChannel 2632-2635 → state listener), and a momentary network drop (1377-1379).
rootCause: onPlaybackStateChanged → STATE_BUFFERING calls showBufferingOverlay(true) immediately, no delay/debounce (1128-1130). The network-disconnect branch (1379) also shows it immediately. tuneToChannel (2632-2636) does setMediaItem/prepare/play and lets the state listener flash the spinner with no smoothing or banner-only path during the zap. CLAUDE.md's own v3.6.4 notes record a real customer 'cycling spinner' report on AFTKRT WiFi where recovery was 300-1000ms but the spinner flashed every recovery — and the spinner-suppression UX was explicitly deferred.
fix: Debounce: on STATE_BUFFERING, post a delayed (~600-800ms) runnable to show the spinner; cancel it on STATE_READY (and on the network-reconnect prepare). Suppress the spinner entirely for the first ~1s of a channel zap (the channel banner already shows at +500ms via showChannelBanner at 2651 — let that cover the gap). Pair with hold-last-frame so the brief gap shows the prior frame, not black.
benchmark: YouTube TV / Netflix keep a pre-buffer that absorbs sub-second dips invisibly and only reveal a buffering indicator after a sustained stall (~1s+), never on routine BUFFERING↔READY churn. Applies to IPTV.
correction: Confirmed — no debounce exists; showBufferingOverlay(true) fires synchronously on STATE_BUFFERING at three independent sites (1129, 1379, and indirectly via tuneToChannel). The buffer-storm detector (1131-1149) addresses the DECODER, not spinner visibility — so it does not mitigate this. P2 is the right severity (visual noise, not an interruption to playback). alreadyHandled=false; the v3.6.4 notes confirm it was knowingly deferred.

title: Mid-stream rebuffer recovery does a full stop()/restart that discards buffer and blacks the screen even for a recoverable blip
symptom: On a sustained network slowdown (the common single-bitrate IPTV case), instead of the picture pausing and resuming where it left off, the screen goes black and the stream visibly cold-restarts/reconnects — a heavier interruption than the dip warranted.
trigger: VOD/Series buffering that exceeds STALL_TIMEOUT_VOD_MS (30s) or LIVE exceeding STALL_TIMEOUT_LIVE_MS (15s) while retries remain — the customer-side bandwidth-bottleneck case (13-15s refills).
rootCause: startStallDetector() (1492-1519) calls p.stop() (1505), delay(delayMs), then p.prepare()/play() (1507-1508). stop() releases the decoder/surface output → black AND discards already-buffered data, forcing a cold re-prepare from the network. For single-bitrate IPTV there's no lower rung to drop to, so the re-prepare just re-incurs the same cold-start latency the dip caused.
fix: For VOD/Series, prefer letting ExoPlayer keep buffering (it self-heals BUFFERING→READY when bytes arrive) and escalate at the timeout to a soft seekTo(currentPosition) rather than stop()/prepare(), preserving the surface and avoiding a full network cold-start. Reserve stop()/re-prepare for cases where the source is truly dead (cause chain shows connection-refused/EOF). Combine with hold-last-frame.
benchmark: Netflix/Prime continue filling the buffer on a stall and resume from the exact paused frame; they don't tear down and re-establish the whole pipeline for a transient dip.
correction: Confirmed the p.stop()/prepare() pattern at 1505-1508. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED P2→P3. Reason: the 30s VOD / 15s LIVE timeouts are deliberately long, so by the time stop() fires, ExoPlayer has already been visibly stuck buffering (spinner on black) for the full timeout — it was NOT silently riding through a 'recoverable blip.' At that point the stream genuinely isn't progressing, and a stop/re-prepare is a defensible (if blunt) recovery, not the cause of the interruption. The auditor over-states the frequency ('the common case'); on a healthy connection this never fires. The real residual harm is narrow: discarding the partial buffer that DID accumulate, making the cold-restart slightly slower than continuing to load. That's polish-tier, hence P3. The hold-last-frame fix (finding #1) already covers the black-screen portion of this symptom; the remaining buffer-discard nuance is minor. Note the LIVE path is also somewhat moot — live streams are append-only with no resume buffer to preserve, so stop()/prepare() costs little there.

title: onPause + 5s autosave save currentPosition with no state/monotonic guard — buffering/errored/rebuild exit overwrites a good resume point with ~0
symptom: Customer watches a movie to 1h30m, the stream rebuffers or hits a decoder-rebuild (flaky-network Fire Stick), they press Back during the spinner. Next launch from Continue Watching replays from the beginning (or a few seconds in) instead of 1h30m. Progress silently regressed.
trigger: Pressing Back / backgrounding while player is in STATE_BUFFERING / STATE_IDLE / error-retry, OR within the rebuild window of rebuildPlayerWithSoftwareDecoder/FfmpegVideo/FfmpegPreferred (new player has setMediaItem+prepare done but seekTo(currentPosition) not yet applied, so currentPosition reads ~0). The concurrent 5s autosave loop (line 977-993) and onPause (line 2950-2961) both read currentPosition with only a dur>0 and pct>0.05 gate.
rootCause: Verified: onPause (2950-2961) and the 5s loop (980-991) both compute pct = pos/dur and save whenever dur>0 && pct>0.05f, with NO check that playbackState==STATE_READY and NO monotonic floor against the last persisted position. saveProgress() (PlayerViewModel:85-111) builds a fresh WatchProgressEntity (lastWatched defaults to now) and calls watchProgressDao.upsert = @Insert(OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE) (WatchProgressDao:35), which fully REPLACES the existing row — clobbering position, progressPercent AND completed. The rebuild paths capture currentPosition before release then setMediaItem+prepare and only seekTo afterward (line 1929-1931), so during that async window currentPosition genuinely reads ~0; the autosave loop runs on an independent coroutine and can fire mid-rebuild. onDestroyView does NOT save — onPause is the sole authoritative exit-save, so its un-gated save is the real exposure.
fix: Gate every save: only capture/persist currentPosition when player.playbackState == STATE_READY (or playWhenReady && pos>0); and make the bookmark monotonic — fetch the prior persisted position and refuse to write a position that regresses more than a tolerance (~15s) unless the user explicitly seeked back. Skip the save entirely during an active rebuild (a usingSoftwareVideoDecoder/rebuildInProgress flag). Keep completed/95% logic intact. This makes resume monotonic and immune to the dominant 'Back while a spinner is up' exit.
benchmark: Netflix/Disney+ checkpoint only from a known-good playing state and treat the bookmark as monotonic within a session — a transient buffer or decoder hiccup never rewinds your resume point. (Server-authoritative bookmark in their case; here the fix is a client-side state-gate + monotonic floor, which fully applies to single-bitrate IPTV.)
correction: CONFIRMED as the auditor described, with one nuance: the auditor frames NonCancellable as 'making the bug worse' — that is accurate but secondary. NonCancellable only guarantees the onPause write lands; the 5s autosave loop is an equally likely (often more likely) corruptor because it fires every 5s regardless of player state, including mid-rebuild, with no Back-press needed. The most damaging path is actually: user is mid-movie, a decoder rebuild fires (mt8695 watchdog ladder is common on this exact hardware), the autosave loop ticks during the prepare→seek window and persists ~0 with completed=false — no user action at all. P0 is correct; if anything the auditor under-credited the autosave-loop path.

title: Hard Resume/Play-from-Beginning modal on every detail/hero/recommendation play — friction Netflix never imposes
symptom: Pressing Play on a movie/episode from its detail page (or Home hero, or a recommendation) pops a blocking 'You stopped at 1:24:05. Would you like to resume or start over?' AlertDialog that must be answered before anything plays. Slower to picture and feels like the app second-guessing the customer. For series binge, you get prompted on every episode.
trigger: Any play from VodDetailFragment (playButton, line 128), SeriesDetailFragment.playEpisode (line 323), Home hero / recommendation via playVodWithResumeCheck (HomeFragment lines 739/1034/1150/1840 → 1876), whenever progress exists (>5% and not completed). ONLY the Continue Watching card path (navigateToContinueWatching, line 1789) resumes silently.
rootCause: Verified: ResumePlaybackHelper.showIfNeeded() unconditionally builds a blocking android.app.AlertDialog when progress exists (>0.05, not completed). It's wired into all three detail/hero/recommendation paths but deliberately bypassed by navigateToContinueWatching, which goes straight to the player and resumes via the setMediaItem(uri, positionMs) path. So the app ships two contradictory resume UXs and the higher-traffic detail path is the friction-heavy one.
fix: Make resume silent by default on all paths — pass the saved position through to the player (it already resumes via getResumePositionSync→setMediaItem(uri, positionMs)). Replace the upfront modal with an in-player affordance: a ~5s 'Resuming from 1:24:05 — press DOWN to restart' chip plus a persistent 'Restart' control in PlayerControlsBar. Keep ResumePlaybackHelper only as an opt-in setting.
benchmark: Netflix/Disney+/Prime resume instantly with no prompt and surface a small 'Restart'/'From Beginning' control inside the player. This applies cleanly to single-bitrate IPTV — it's a UX pattern, not an ABR feature.
correction: CONFIRMED exactly as described. The silent-resume machinery already exists and is proven on the Continue Watching card path (setMediaItem(uri, positionMs) at line 420 + forceStartFromBeginning arg plumbing), so the fix is low-risk — it just needs the detail/hero/recommendation paths to stop calling showIfNeeded and pass position through. P1 is correct.

title: Binge 'Up Next' Continue Watching row shows a phantom ~6% progress bar (progressPercent=0.06 / duration=1)
symptom: After finishing an episode, the never-watched next episode appears in Continue Watching with a thin gold progress bar (~6%), as if partly watched, before the customer has ever opened it.
trigger: Series binge completion: STATE_ENDED (or advanceSeriesOnCompletion) inserts the next episode as an Up Next entry.
rootCause: Verified: advanceSeriesOnCompletion() writes WatchProgressEntity(position=0, duration=1, progressPercent=0.06f) (PlayerViewModel:170-179). The 0.06 is a hack to clear getContinueWatching's 'progressPercent > 0.05' filter. ContinueWatchingPresenter sets progressBar.progress = (progressPercent*100).toInt() = 6 UNCONDITIONALLY (line 42) and NEVER hides the bar, so the phantom 6% bar renders.
fix: Detect the queued/up-next case in the presenter (it already computes isUpNext = isSeries && position==0L at line 46) and hide the progress bar (progressBar.visibility = GONE) for it, OR add an explicit queued flag to WatchProgressEntity, broaden the getContinueWatching filter to include queued rows (drop the 0.06 hack, store progressPercent=0f), and have the presenter show only the 'Up Next' badge with no bar. Guard the bar against duration<=0 / position==0 regardless.
benchmark: Netflix's Up Next card shows the new episode with NO progress bar and an 'Episode N / Next Episode' label — never a phantom partial-progress indicator.
correction: PARTIALLY confirmed; auditor OVERSTATED severity and one symptom. (1) The phantom 6% bar is real — confirmed, presenter never hides the bar. (2) BUT the claimed 'nonsensical time-left value / broken time-left math' is NOT real: with duration=1 and position=0, minutesLeft = (1-0)/60000 = 0, and the presenter hides the time-left label at line 72 (`if (minutesLeft > 0)`), so no bad time-left text is shown. (3) The presenter ALSO already shows a correct 'S1 E2 · Up Next' label (lines 46-52) via the isUpNext = position==0L check — the auditor missed that partial handling exists. Net: this is a single cosmetic phantom-bar glitch on a queued card, not a metadata-corruption bug. Downgraded P2→P3. position=0 means playback itself correctly starts at the top (getResumePositionSync returns 0), so zero functional impact.

title: Resume position never re-validated against actual stream duration — can park on a black/ended end frame on a re-encoded shorter IPTV VOD
symptom: Rarely, a movie 'resumes' to a black/frozen end frame or jumps straight to the ended state, forcing the customer to scrub back manually.
trigger: The IPTV server re-encodes / swaps the backing file behind a streamId so the new stream is shorter than when the position was saved, then the user resumes. The stored position now exceeds the new stream's length.
rootCause: Verified: getResumePositionSync() returns progress.position with no upper bound (PlayerViewModel:77-83); the call site applies only coerceAtLeast(0L) (line 418) and passes it to setMediaItem(uri, resumePos). There is NO post-STATE_READY revalidation against the now-known duration anywhere in the fragment (grep of duration/coerce/clamp confirms only seek-clamps at 2417/2484, none on the resume path). ExoPlayer internally clamps a start position beyond duration to the period end, so it lands at the end rather than crashing — but 'lands at the end' is the bad outcome.
fix: After STATE_READY when duration is known, if the resumed startPos is within the last ~10s of (or beyond) duration, treat it as stale/completed and restart from 0 (or seek to duration-30s). Optionally store the saved duration and discard the resume if the new actual duration differs by more than a tolerance.
benchmark: Streaming platforms validate the bookmark against the current asset runtime and fall back to a sane position (or mark complete) rather than parking on a black end frame.
correction: CONFIRMED mechanically (no upper clamp, no revalidation), but rarity is correctly reflected in P3. The precondition — server mutating the backing file behind the same streamId between the save and the resume, to a SHORTER length — is genuinely uncommon. ExoPlayer's internal clamp prevents a crash, so the worst case is a black end frame the user scrubs back from. Severity P3 is right; not a flawlessness-defining defect.

title: No next-episode pre-buffering — black gap + spinner between every episode
symptom: Episode ends (or user taps 'Watch Next'), the SurfaceView clears to black, a bare centered indeterminate ProgressBar appears, and 2-5s later (on a 1GB Fire TV / single-bitrate IPTV cold buffer fill) the next episode's first frame paints. The transition is felt on every auto-advance — not the seamless cross-fade Netflix/Disney+ post-play gives.
trigger: Every binge auto-advance: the countdown reaching zero (BingeCountdownOverlay.onFinish -> onPlayNext), pressing 'Watch Next' on the card, or the Next-Episode control (skipToNextEpisode). Worst on slow-throughput connections and budget Fire Sticks where cold buffer fill is slowest.
rootCause: Both auto-advance paths load the next episode synchronously into the SAME ExoPlayer/SurfaceView: player.setMediaItem(MediaItem.fromUri(next.url)) -> player.prepare() -> player.play() (lines 490-492 in the binge onPlayNext, 2344-2346 in skipToNextEpisode). Verified via grep that there is NO ConcatenatingMediaSource / addMediaItem / setMediaItems / seekToNextMediaItem / preload / prefetch anywhere in the player package — the search returns zero hits. So the next stream is fetched/demuxed/decoded entirely from cold at the transition moment. The prepare() puts the player into STATE_BUFFERING, which calls showBufferingOverlay(true) (line 1129) -> a plain ProgressBar over a now-black surface (no frame for the new media yet). The 15s binge-window runway (line 1003) is used ONLY to render the countdown card, never to pre-prepare the next item.
fix: Use the binge window as a pre-buffer runway: when the next episode is resolved at the 15s mark (line 1005), build/append it to the timeline (player.addMediaItem(nextMediaItem) on a queued player, or ConcatenatingMediaSource2) so ExoPlayer pre-buffers it while the current episode plays; on auto-advance call player.seekToNextMediaItem() instead of setMediaItem+prepare so the transition is into an already-buffered item with no cold load. Lighter interim: hold the last decoded frame under a dimmed scrim during the new item's buffer instead of going to black.
benchmark: Netflix/Disney+/Prime post-play have the next episode buffered before the current one ends and cross-fade in — never black, never a spinner. This applies even to single-bitrate IPTV: ABR is irrelevant here, the win is pre-preparing the known next URL during the dwell window, not bitrate adaptation.
correction: Confirmed exactly as reported. Existing hardening does NOT cover this: resume-via-setMediaItem(item, positionMs) and BufferConfigs only affect the CURRENT item's load, never pre-buffer the next. The grep claim is accurate. Severity P1 is correct — it degrades every boundary but doesn't break watching.

title: resolveNextEpisode() does an uncached network round-trip (hit up to 3x per boundary), delaying the prompt and risking a false 'no more episodes'
symptom: On a slow or briefly-glitchy IPTV connection the binge card / next title appears late, and in the worst case the countdown completes, fires play-next, and a single transient network failure causes 'No more episodes' (line 2355) or the series-complete overlay (line 501/1009) to fire on an episode that actually HAS a next one — the binge silently stops.
trigger: Reaching the end of any series episode on a slow/intermittent connection. Risk compounds because the lookup runs multiple times per boundary and ANY single failure collapses to 'no next episode'.
rootCause: resolveNextEpisode() (PlayerViewModel:219) calls contentRepository.getSeriesInfo(seriesId), which is a raw getApi().getSeriesInfo(...) Retrofit call with NO caching (ContentRepository:75-78). VERIFIED the OkHttpClient.Builder in NetworkModule:44-67 has no .cache(...) configured — there is no HTTP disk cache at all, and no session/Room cache for series info, so every call is a fresh network fetch of the full series payload. PlayerViewModel holds only scalar series context (seriesId/seasonNum/episodeNum, lines 41-43) — it has no in-memory episode list, so it must re-fetch every time. resolveNextEpisode runs at 3 independent sites per boundary: binge overlay show (Fragment:1005), the chosen advance path (Fragment:481 onPlayNext OR :2335 skipToNextEpisode), and advanceSeriesOnCompletion on STATE_ENDED (PlayerViewModel:164). The function is wrapped in try/catch returning null on ANY exception (lines 256-258), so a transient failure during the countdown is indistinguishable from 'episodes list exhausted'.
fix: Cache getSeriesInfo per seriesId for the playback session (or Room) so 2nd/3rd lookups are instant and resilient; resolve the next episode ONCE (at play start or the binge window) and stash the NextEpisodeResult for onPlayNext/advance to reuse. Distinguish 'no next episode' (episodes list parsed, current is last) from 'lookup threw' — on a thrown failure, retry briefly and keep the binge card up rather than firing 'No more episodes' / series-complete.
benchmark: Netflix has the episode list and next-episode metadata client-side before the episode starts; the decision is local and instantaneous. This benchmark legitimately applies — it's about caching the metadata the app already fetched in SeriesDetailFragment, not about ABR.
correction: Confirmed and slightly strengthened: there is not only no result cache, there is no OkHttp disk cache either (NetworkModule:44-67 has no .cache()), so even back-to-back identical calls re-hit the network. The null-on-exception conflation (PlayerViewModel:256-258) is the genuinely customer-hurting part: a flaky-IPTV blip ends an active binge with a wrong 'finished the season' message. The 'IO dispatcher so non-blocking' mitigation the auditor noted is real but irrelevant to the false-stop outcome. P1 is correct.

title: Episode ends to a black/idle player with no auto-play and no completion UI when the binge window is missed OR the user cancelled the binge card
symptom: An episode finishes and nothing happens — no next episode, no countdown card, no series-complete screen. The viewer is left on a black/idle player and must press Back manually, unsure whether the binge broke.
trigger: TWO reachable paths land here, not one. (a) The 1s position poll never observes (dur-pos) < 15000 before STATE_ENDED — duration reported 0/unknown until the very end, a buffering stall over the final 15s, a hard cut to STATE_ENDED, or wrong/missing IPTV duration metadata; bingeShown stays false. (b) [MISSED by auditor] The user presses 'Cancel' on the binge card ('not now, let me finish'); bingeShown was already latched true at line 1004 and is NEVER reset in onCancel (line 505), so when the episode then reaches STATE_ENDED there is no terminal UX at all.
rootCause: The ONLY trigger that auto-plays the next episode or shows the series-complete overlay is the poll at line 1003 (dur>0 && pos>0 && (dur-pos)<15000 && !bingeShown). STATE_ENDED for SERIES (line 1188-1192) calls ONLY advanceSeriesOnCompletion(), which inserts an 'Up Next' DB row (PlayerViewModel:161-181) — it does NOT auto-play and does NOT show seriesCompleteOverlay. Contrast VOD STATE_ENDED (line 1194-1203) which at least shows Watch Next or pops back; SERIES has no equivalent in-player terminal UX. So both the missed-window case and the cancelled-card case (bingeShown never reset at line 505) dead-end on a black/idle player. The DB Up Next row only helps the Home screen's Continue Watching, not the in-session viewer.
fix: In STATE_ENDED for SERIES, when the in-player binge UX never ran (e.g. seriesCompleteOverlay not showing and no auto-advance issued), drive the same decision there: resolve next episode (reusing the cached NextEpisodeResult from finding #2) and either auto-advance OR show seriesCompleteOverlay — never a silent black end. Also reset bingeShown=false in onCancel (line 505) and re-check the binge window once duration becomes known for unknown-duration streams, so the credits-watcher still gets a completion screen.
benchmark: Netflix always lands an episode end on post-play autoplay OR a clear 'You've finished this season' screen — never a frozen/black player with no next action.
correction: [MISSED] The auditor framed this as only triggering on broken/unknown duration metadata (relatively rare). Verified a SECOND, more common path to the identical dead-end: pressing 'Cancel' on the binge card. onCancel (line 505) is a no-op comment ('Stay on current episode') and never resets bingeShown (confirmed: bingeShown is only reset at lines 488 and 2342, both auto-advance paths). So any user who declines auto-play to finish the episode/credits then hits STATE_ENDED -> DB-row-only -> black dead-end. This makes the hole more reachable than reported; P2 is still appropriate (friction, not a watch-breaking crash) but the fix must include resetting bingeShown on cancel.

title: Binge transition uses a bare spinner over black + a Toast — no last-frame hold, no branded next-up card
symptom: Even when the next episode loads fast, the in-between moment looks unfinished: black surface + generic centered indeterminate ProgressBar (the same one used for any mid-stream rebuffer), with the next episode only confirmed by a small Toast. Reads as 'cheap/loading' rather than a deliberate next-up moment.
trigger: Every binge auto-advance and manual 'Watch Next' — the window between the current episode being torn down and the next episode's first frame.
rootCause: showBufferingOverlay (2151-2169) programmatically adds a plain WRAP_CONTENT centered ProgressBar with no scrim, no next-episode artwork, no 'Now Playing S_E_' card — identical to any rebuffer spinner. Next-episode confirmation is Toast.makeText(next.name) at lines 499 and 2353. The binge card itself (BingeCountdownOverlay) shows only the title text + countdown with no poster/thumbnail (verified: it inflates overlay_binge_countdown with binge_next_title TextView, no ImageView for episode art).
fix: During a binge transition, replace the generic spinner with a dedicated 'Up Next' card: next-episode title + S/E + poster thumbnail over a dimmed last-frame, with the buffering indicator integrated. Drop the redundant Toast. Combined with finding #1's pre-buffer, this turns the boundary into an intentional branded moment.
benchmark: Netflix/Disney+ show a styled next-episode title/thumbnail post-play card and cross-fade into already-buffered video. Valid as a polish target.
correction: Confirmed as reported; P3 is correct (pure polish gap, not a functional hiccup). Note this finding is largely a cosmetic restatement of #1's symptom — its standalone value is low until #1's pre-buffer lands, since masking a 2-5s black load with a prettier card without pre-buffering still leaves the customer waiting. Bumped the auditor's medium confidence to high on the code facts (the spinner/Toast/no-thumbnail claims are all verified).

title: Disabled/fallback audio state leaks from one episode to the next in a binge
symptom: During a series binge, if one episode hits the Stage-2 audio-disable fallback (hardware codec error with no alternate track and no FFmpeg), the next auto-advanced episode also plays with no sound even though its audio is decodable, and stays silent for the rest of the binge until the customer backs fully out of the player and re-enters.
trigger: SERIES playback where episode N reaches Stage-2 audio disable (audioDisabledByFallback=true at line 1055/1068), then auto-advances to N+1 via the binge countdown onPlayNext (line 478-503) or the skip-next button (glue.onNextEpisode -> skipToNextEpisode, line 2332/3026).
rootCause: Both episode-transition paths call setMediaItem/prepare/play on the SAME shared ExoPlayer but never reset audioFallbackAttempted / audioDisabledByFallback / userTrackOverrideActive / mtkMultichannelFfmpegApplied, and never clear the setTrackTypeDisabled(AUDIO,true) override Stage-2 applied (line 1058/1074). onTracksChanged then early-returns at line 1294 (`if (audioDisabledByFallback) return`), so the new episode's audio is never selected. The audio-reset block exists in exactly three places — tuneToChannel (2599-2617, LIVE only), showErrorDialog retry (2179-2189), showFriendlyError retry (2302-2311) — and was never wired into the SERIES next-episode/binge transitions.
fix: Extract the reset block (audioFallbackAttempted=false, audioDisabledByFallback=false, userTrackOverrideActive=false, mtkMultichannelFfmpegApplied=false, plus trackSelector setTrackTypeDisabled(AUDIO,false)+clearOverridesOfType(AUDIO) exactly like 2185-2189) into a resetAudioStateForNewContent() helper and call it at the top of both skipToNextEpisode() (2332) and the binge onPlayNext advance (478) before setMediaItem.
benchmark: Netflix/Disney+ treat each episode as an independent session with fresh decoder negotiation; a codec quirk on one episode never carries audio state into the next.
correction: CONFIRMED with one severity-scoping nuance the auditor overstated. The leak ONLY bites when Stage-2 (disable audio, lines 1055/1068) actually fires — i.e. a hard ERROR_CODE_AUDIO_TRACK_* PlaybackException with no alternate track AND no FFmpeg available. If Stage-1.5 rebuildPlayerWithFfmpegPreferred() succeeds (the common AC3/EAC3 mt8695 case), audio is rerouted through FFmpeg and audioDisabledByFallback stays false, so the next episode is NOT muted. Since AudioLogger.isFfmpegAvailable is true on virtually all shipping ARM builds (the FFmpeg AAR loads on all primary devices), Stage-2 is comparatively rare — it needs FFmpeg to be unavailable OR to also fail. So 'one bad episode silently mutes EVERY subsequent episode' is real but narrower than implied. Separately, userTrackOverrideActive leaking is a real secondary bug (manual track pick on episode N persists the override-protection flag into N+1, suppressing English auto-select). P1 stands because when it does hit, it's a multi-episode silent break with no in-player recovery.

title: Mid-stream audio dropout (sink error / sustained stall) is logged but never recovered
symptom: Mid-movie or mid-channel the audio cuts out and stays silent while video keeps playing; the customer must manually back out and re-open, or change channel, to get sound back. On an AudioTrack sink error or a sustained audio-renderer stall the silence persists for the session.
trigger: onAudioSinkError (non-fatal, bypasses onPlayerError entirely) or a sustained audio stall where audioDecoderCounters.renderedOutputBufferCount stops advancing for >10s while video continues (checkAudioStall, PlaybackHealthMonitor:190-228).
rootCause: checkAudioStall() only calls logger.logAppEvent("AUDIO_STALL") — PlaybackHealthMonitor's constructor takes only (logger, scope) with no fragment callback, so it structurally cannot trigger recovery. onAudioSinkError/onAudioUnderrun/onAudioDisabled in ExoPlayerDiagnosticListener are AnalyticsListener callbacks that are pure logger.logAppEvent() calls. The three-stage audio fallback ladder lives entirely inside corePlayerListener.onPlayerError (1018-1082) and only triggers on PlaybackException via isAudioDecoderError(); a non-fatal sink error never reaches onPlayerError, so nothing attempts recovery.
fix: Add an onAudioStall callback into PlaybackHealthMonitor (and wire onAudioSinkError) that does a lightweight recovery: toggle setTrackTypeDisabled(AUDIO,false)+re-select, or escalate to rebuildPlayerWithFfmpegPreferred() preserving position, with an attempt-cap/debounce. Already correctly gated on hasSelectedAudio && volume>0 (lines 194-198), so muted preview/audio-only won't false-trigger.
benchmark: Netflix/YouTube TV silently re-initialize the audio decoder on a sink fault and refill — the dropout is a sub-second blip, not a permanent loss, and the viewer never has to restart.
correction: CONFIRMED root cause and gap exactly. Lowered P1->P2: this is a genuine hole but the customer-felt FREQUENCY is low. Real Ooustream triage (per CLAUDE.md debug-log reference) shows AUDIO_UNDERRUN/AUDIO_DISABLED/AUDIO_SINK_ERROR overwhelmingly ride on top of NETWORK STARVATION — the audio chain tearing down because data isn't arriving — not standalone codec/sink faults. In the starvation case, recovery has nothing to recover (the pipe is the problem) and toggling the renderer would just thrash. A true permanent-silence-with-healthy-video onAudioSinkError (e.g. a Reelz ad-break elementary-stream swap) does exist and is unrecovered, but it's a minority of the logged audio events. Worth fixing, but P1 overstates how often a paying customer hits irrecoverable mid-stream silence vs. a network-driven blip that resolves on its own.

title: Anti-pop mute on channel switch is defeated by synchronous volume restore
symptom: On a live channel zap, a brief audible click/blip of the new stream's first audio buffer can be heard at full volume because the intended mute window has effectively zero duration.
trigger: Every live channel switch via tuneToChannel (lines 2630-2636).
rootCause: tuneToChannel sets player.volume=0f (2631), then setMediaItem/prepare/play (2633-2635), then player.volume=1f (2636) — all synchronously on the same main-thread call stack. The player spends no real wall-clock time muted; volume is back to 1f before the new stream decodes its first audio buffer, so any first-buffer click is unmuted.
fix: Set volume=0f before setMediaItem, restore to 1f from onPlaybackStateChanged STATE_READY (or onRenderedFirstFrame) for the new item with a ~600ms safety timeout, ideally an 80-120ms fade-in. Apply the same pattern to skipToNextEpisode/binge if a click is observed there.
benchmark: Netflix/YouTube TV hard-gate or crossfade audio across a source switch so the new audio fades up only once it is actually decoding — zero pop.
correction: CONFIRMED the code does nothing (synchronous mute/unmute) but the auditor MISDESCRIBED the artifact and OVERSTATED scope. (1) WRONG: 'pop of the PREVIOUS stream's audio' — setMediaItem tears down the old pipeline immediately, so there is no previous-stream audio left to leak; the only possible artifact is the NEW stream's first un-faded buffer (a minor click), and on a channel switch the new stream enters STATE_BUFFERING for hundreds of ms before any audio renders, so in practice the pop is faint-to-inaudible on most streams. (2) WRONG: 'and on VOD resume' — VERIFIED the VOD/SERIES initial-load path (lines 413-430) does NOT mute at all; there is no resume-mute to be defeated. The artifact is purely the live-zap path. Severity lowered P2->P3: a faint occasional click on channel change is polish-tier, not felt friction, and IPTV zaps already carry a >1s buffering gap that dominates the perception.

title: Every D-pad seek tap fires an immediate network seek — no scrub accumulation/debounce
symptom: Tapping Left/Right repeatedly to skip past the currently-buffered window produces a stutter-then-spinner on each press that lands outside the buffer, rather than one fluid scrub. Within the buffered window (VOD 15-45s ahead, 10-30s low-mem) seeks are instant; the storm only manifests when stepping repeatedly beyond it.
trigger: User presses DPAD_LEFT/RIGHT (or FF/RW, swipe, double-tap) several times in a row on VOD/Series, each step landing past the buffered range.
rootCause: Confirmed in code: every seek path commits player.seekTo() synchronously on ACTION_DOWN with no pending-target accumulation. Glue onKey DPAD_LEFT/RIGHT (262/272) calls playerAdapter.seekTo immediately; PlayerControlsBar.dispatchKeyEvent (641/647) invokes onDpadSeek which seeks at fragment 832; FF/RW (241/250), swipe (2484/2487) and double-tap all seekTo() directly. seekDeltaForRepeat (glue 354, bar 656) only grows the STEP (10s→30s→60s), not coalesces commits. No pendingSeek/debounce/OnSeekBarChangeListener exists anywhere in the module.
fix: Accumulate pendingSeekTargetMs on each press, update the seekbar/time text optimistically, and commit a single player.seekTo() after ~250-350ms idle or on key-up. Pairs naturally with CLOSEST_SYNC (see seek-exact-params) so the one committed seek is also cheap.
benchmark: Netflix/YouTube TV accumulate the scrub target while a direction is held and commit one seek on release — picture refetches once, at the landing point. This DOES apply to single-bitrate IPTV: it's about coalescing seek commits, not ABR.
correction: Severity corrected P1→P2. The auditor's '8 taps to skip an intro' is overstated: seekDeltaForRepeat accelerates to 30s after 3 presses and 60s after 10, so a 60-90s intro skip is typically 2-4 presses, and any step that lands inside the 15-45s VOD / 10-30s low-mem buffer (BufferConfigs.kt) is instant with no refetch. Also note seek-induced BUFFERING is correctly insulated from the recovery ladder — the stall detector only fires after a 30s VOD timeout (fragment 1499) and the frame watchdog is deliberately not restarted on seek BUFFERING→READY (fragment 1156-1159) — so a seek storm degrades smoothness but never escalates into retries/error dialogs. Real and worth fixing, but it's friction, not an interruption.

title: No setSeekParameters() — every seek is frame-EXACT, maximizing decode-from-keyframe cost
symptom: After a seek that lands outside the buffer, motion resumes a beat later than necessary because the decoder must walk from the preceding keyframe to the exact frame before rendering — more pronounced on the weak MTK decoders in Fire Stick targets.
trigger: Any VOD/Series seek (D-pad, FF/RW, swipe, double-tap, chapter jump) that lands outside the buffered range.
rootCause: Confirmed: all four ExoPlayer.Builder sites (305, 1867, 1987, 2075) omit setSeekParameters(), so SeekParameters.DEFAULT (frame-exact) is in force. grep for setSeekParameters/SeekParameters returns zero hits across the whole module. On long-GOP IPTV-transcoded streams the keyframe→target decode is real added latency on coarse D-pad scrubs the user can't perceive the precision of anyway.
fix: Set SeekParameters.CLOSEST_SYNC (or PREVIOUS_SYNC) during active coarse scrubbing so the picture snaps to the nearest keyframe and resumes immediately; keep EXACT only for the final landing commit and for resume/chapter jumps. Cheap one-liner per build site (or set once and re-apply on rebuilds).
benchmark: Streaming players seek to keyframe boundaries during active scrub for near-instant resume, reserving frame-exact for the final commit. Applies to single-bitrate IPTV — it's a decode-cost reduction, not ABR.
correction: Severity corrected P1→P2. Real and code-grounded, but the magnitude is GOP-dependent and only felt on out-of-buffer seeks; for the common in-buffer step it's invisible. Note the resume path (fragment 418-423) uses setMediaItem(uri, resumePos) which buffers from the offset — frame-exactness there is desirable for landing on the right spot, so a blanket CLOSEST_SYNC must be scoped to active-scrub only, not applied to resume/chapter (the auditor's fix correctly says this).

title: Seek-induced rebuffer shows a bare spinner over a frozen frame instead of an invisible refill
symptom: A bare indeterminate spinner pops over the last frame the instant a seek lands outside the buffer, then vanishes — routine scrubbing looks like the stream is struggling even when the refill is ~1s. Rapid scrubbing flashes it repeatedly.
trigger: Any seek (or transient auto-recovery) that briefly enters STATE_BUFFERING.
rootCause: Confirmed: onPlaybackStateChanged → STATE_BUFFERING calls showBufferingOverlay(true) unconditionally and synchronously (1129). showBufferingOverlay (2151-2169) lazily inflates a plain indeterminate ProgressBar and toggles VISIBLE — no postDelayed grace window, no distinction between a sub-second seek refill and a genuine stall. STATE_READY (1152) hides it promptly, so it does clear fast, but every short refill flashes it.
fix: Gate showBufferingOverlay(true) behind a ~400-600ms postDelayed that is cancelled if STATE_READY arrives first, so sub-threshold seek refills hold the last frame with no chrome; only persistent buffering shows the spinner. This is precisely the v3.6.4-deferred 'suppress spinner during <1s recoveries' item.
benchmark: Netflix/Disney+ hold the last frame on a brief seek refill with no spinner; chrome appears only once the stall is long enough the user would think it froze.
correction: Confirmed real; severity P2 appropriate (kept as filed). The CLAUDE.md v3.6.4 note explicitly logged this spinner-suppression as deferred and it was never shipped — verified there is no grace-window delay in showBufferingOverlay. One nuance: the same unconditional spinner also flashes on every channel-switch/recovery BUFFERING, so the fix benefits live zap perception too, not just seeking.

title: No scrub preview thumbnails or absolute scrub-time bubble — only a relative '+Ns' text
symptom: While scrubbing, the customer can't see WHERE they'll land — no filmstrip thumbnail and no absolute timecode bubble at the thumb, only a cumulative '+30s'/'-30s' delta. Finding a specific scene is seek-watch-seek-watch.
trigger: User scrubs a movie/episode to find a specific point.
rootCause: Confirmed: the only scrub feedback is SeekFeedbackOverlay's centered cumulative '+Ns' text (showSeek accumulates cumulativeDeltaMs, 36-57) — relative, not absolute. updatePosition (276-285) only sets the seekbar progress + time-left/right text. No PlaybackSeekDataProvider / thumbnail sprite source is wired anywhere (grep returns zero hits). The seekbar is enabled+focusable for D-pad but has no OnSeekBarChangeListener and no preview affordance.
fix: Short term (cheap, high value): render the ABSOLUTE target timecode of the pending seek (e.g. '1:23:45') at/near the seekbar thumb during scrub — pairs with the pendingSeekTarget from seek-no-debounce-storm. Long term where CPU/bandwidth allow: client-side low-res keyframe thumbnails (or a server BIF if flarecoral ever exposes one) via Leanback PlaybackSeekDataProvider.
benchmark: Netflix/Prime/YouTube TV show a live thumbnail filmstrip plus a timecode while scrubbing so you land on the right scene first try.
correction: Confirmed real, P3 (polish) is correct — true trickplay thumbnails are genuinely impractical for single-bitrate Xtream VOD on a 1GB Fire Stick, so the realistic win is the absolute-timecode bubble, which the auditor correctly prioritizes. Minor cite correction: the auditor described the seekbar at PlayerControlsBar.kt:223-226 as 'non-interactive (a progress indicator)', but those exact lines actually set seekBar.isEnabled = true and isFocusable = true (for D-pad focus). The substance holds — there is no touch OnSeekBarChangeListener and no scrub preview — but the 'non-interactive' phrasing and that specific line cite are imprecise.

title: Watchdog 720p/480p downgrade + software-decoder rebuild is permanent — never cleared, so the rest of the live session stays downscaled and CPU-bound
symptom: After one channel briefly stutters/black-screens and trips the frame watchdog, every channel the user zaps to afterward plays soft/blurry (720p, then 480p) on the slow software decoder — even clean HD channels the same device handled natively seconds earlier. The picture visibly looks worse and never recovers until the user fully backs out of the player and re-enters.
trigger: Live TV: one channel freezes frames for >=3s repeatedly (transient buffering, a momentary decoder hiccup, a bad-encode channel) -> watchdog escalates: SEEK_FLUSH -> rebuildPlayerWithSoftwareDecoder() / rebuildPlayerWithFfmpegVideoDecoder() -> setMaxVideoSize(1280,720) -> setMaxVideoSize(854,480). The user then zaps via debouncedTune -> tuneToChannel, which reuses the SAME player + trackSelector.
rootCause: The recovery ladder is strictly one-directional. trackSelector is created once (line 243) and reused across every rebuild (player builders at 308/870/990/2078 all pass the same trackSelector!!). setMaxVideoSize(720)/(480) is applied to it at lines 1702/1728/1760/1773/1783 and is NEVER cleared — grep for clearVideoSizeConstraints returns zero matches, and there is no setMaxVideoSize(Int.MAX_VALUE,...) anywhere. The fields usingSoftwareVideoDecoder (line 172) and usingFfmpegVideoDecoder (line 178) are set to true (lines 1838/1959/1960) and NEVER set back to false (grep for '= false' on these matches only the declarations). tuneToChannel (2593) resets retryCount/audioFallbackAttempted/mtkMultichannelFfmpegApplied/the watchdog job and re-enables audio (2616), but never touches the video cap, never resets the SW/FFmpeg flags, and never rebuilds back to the hardware factory — it only swaps the MediaItem (2633). So the next channel inherits the SW-rebuilt player and the 480p cap for the entire session.
fix: In tuneToChannel, clear the cap and re-probe hardware: trackSelector.setParameters(buildUponParameters().clearVideoSizeConstraints()), and if usingSoftwareVideoDecoder/usingFfmpegVideoDecoder are set, rebuild once with AudioPipelineFactory.createMtkAwareRenderersFactory and reset both flags to false so the new channel gets a fresh full-resolution HW attempt. Additionally, in the watchdog 'sustained playback confirmed' branch (line 1815), after N good polls clear the cap and attempt ONE upward step to the hardware factory; only fall back again if it re-stalls. Keep the cap sticky ONLY for known-bad MTK (mt8695/mt8167) where HW genuinely never works. The Retry button handler (2178-2189) should also clear the video cap, not just audio overrides.
benchmark: Netflix/YouTube TV continuously re-evaluate decoder + throughput headroom and climb back to the maximum the panel/decoder support within seconds; a momentary dip causes a brief recoverable reduction, never a session-long lock to a low rung, and each new title/channel starts fresh at max attempt instead of inheriting the previous one's emergency downgrade. Note this is NOT an ABR claim (IPTV is single-bitrate) — it is the decoder/resolution axis, which the app really does have and really does abandon permanently.
correction: Confirmed exactly as reported. Line references are slightly off (the 720->480 cap ladder is at 1746-1788 not 1759-1786, tuneToChannel is 2593-2676) but the mechanism is precisely right: cap+SW-factory never cleared, flags never reset, same trackSelector/player reused across zaps via tuneToChannel. The 'sustained playback' reset branch (1815-1821) only resets watchdogResetCount/consecutiveGoodPolls — verified it does NOT clear the cap or the factory. Severity P1 is correct. One scoping note the auditor missed: tuneToChannel DOES cancel and restart the watchdog (2609-2610 + STATE_READY at 1159), so the ladder COUNTER and the local hwDecoderProvenGood var reset per channel — but the persistent cap (on trackSelector) and the SW/FFmpeg fields (instance-level) survive, which is exactly why the downgrade is sticky despite the per-channel watchdog restart. This strengthens, not weakens, the finding.

title: No upward decoder/resolution re-probe after a transient VOD/Series downgrade — the rest of the title plays in SD software decode
symptom: A momentary wifi dip or one frozen-frame event drops a movie to software-decoded 720p/480p, and it stays there for the entire title even after the network/decoder fully recovers seconds later. The customer watches the rest of the movie at materially lower quality with no way to get HD back short of exiting and re-launching playback.
trigger: VOD/Series: brief network starvation or a single decode stall escalates the watchdog to rebuildPlayerWithSoftwareDecoder()/rebuildPlayerWithFfmpegVideoDecoder() + a 720p/480p cap. Because the player isn't recreated mid-title and tuneToChannel only applies to Live, nothing ever re-probes hardware for the rest of the title.
rootCause: Every rebuild call (lines 1615/1647/1683/1704/1766/1775/1785) goes DOWN the ladder to a software/FFmpeg factory; grep confirms there is no rebuildPlayerWithHardware, no clearOverridesOfType(TRACK_TYPE_VIDEO), no reprobe/stepUp/escalateUp logic anywhere in the fragment. The only 'recovery' is the counter reset at 1815-1819 which leaves the applied cap and the software factory in place. For VOD/Series the same player persists for the whole title (no per-channel tuneToChannel path), so the degradation lasts the entire movie.
fix: Add a debounced upward re-probe: after the SW/cap path has sustained smooth playback (e.g. SUSTAINED_PLAYBACK_POLLS x2 = ~12s) AND buffer health is good, do one controlled attempt at the current position — clearVideoSizeConstraints() + rebuild with the hardware factory, resetting usingSoftwareVideoDecoder/usingFfmpegVideoDecoder. If it re-stalls within a short window, fall back and mark the stream confirmed-bad for the rest of the title (don't oscillate). This mirrors ABR step-up logic but on the decoder/resolution axis — valid even though IPTV has no bitrate rungs.
benchmark: Every top platform's quality controller is bidirectional: it backs off on starvation and ramps back up the instant headroom returns, targeting the max the device+panel support. A 5-second dip never costs the rest of the movie in SD. The single-bitrate triage caveat is correctly acknowledged — the missing rung here is decoder/resolution (SW 480p <-> HW native), not ABR.
correction: Confirmed. Verified by grep that NO upward re-probe / hardware-rebuild path exists; the ladder is strictly monotonic-down. The auditor rated this 'medium' confidence — I am raising verifier confidence to high because the code is unambiguous (zero re-probe matches). This overlaps heavily with sticky-resolution-cap (#1) — they share the same root cause (cap+factory never cleared); #1 is the Live-zap manifestation and #2 is the VOD-whole-title manifestation. Both are real and worth keeping distinct because the fixes land in different places (tuneToChannel for Live; the watchdog sustained-playback branch for VOD). P2 is appropriate for the VOD variant since it requires an actual transient stall first (less frequent than zapping).

title: ULTRA_LOW mt8695 devices 'try' HEVC Main 10 they can't decode — but the result is often an indefinite ~3fps FFmpeg slideshow with NO error, not just a delayed friendly error
symptom: On a known-incapable cheap Fire TV Stick (mt8695 / 900MB, e.g. AFTSS), opening a 10-bit HDR HEVC title shows a black screen with a spinner for several seconds while the watchdog churns, and then EITHER surfaces 'This content uses a video format not supported on this device' (the auditor's case) OR — more often — falls into an unwatchable ~3fps FFmpeg software-HEVC slideshow that never errors out, because a slideshow renders frames (just slowly) and so never trips the frozen-frame watchdog. Either way the customer experiences a long broken-looking hang on hardware the app already KNOWS is incapable.
trigger: VOD/Series with HEVC Main 10 (hvc1.2*/hev1.2*) on a device where DeviceTierDetector.canDecodeHevcMain10() returns false (ULTRA_LOW, <1.2GB RAM, mt8695 AFTSS). isKnownBadMtk is true for mt8695, so the watchdog routes to rebuildPlayerWithFfmpegVideoDecoder() at reset=2.
rootCause: v3.7.9 removed the upfront HEVC Main 10 refusal at onTracksChanged (line 1220-1245) — it now only logs HEVC_MAIN10_ATTEMPT and lets hardware try even when canDecodeHevcMain10()==false (1239-1245).
