When HW stalls, the watchdog routes mt8695 to rebuildPlayerWithFfmpegVideoDecoder() at reset=2 (1673-1685). FFmpeg software HEVC on a 4xA53 is ~3fps (acknowledged in CLAUDE.md). The v3.7.0-removed slideshow detector (comment at 1804-1812) means there is NO low-but-nonzero-fps detection: a 3fps slideshow advances frames each 2s poll, so currentFrames != lastRenderedFrameCount, the frozen timer never fires, and the give-up/friendly-error path (1596-1630) is never reached. So the friendly error the auditor credits as the eventual fallback frequently does NOT fire for this exact codec.
fix: Restore a fast-fail for the genuinely-incapable case: in onTracksChanged, when cachedVideoCodecs is HEVC Main 10 AND canDecodeHevcMain10()==false AND tier is ULTRA_LOW, call showFriendlyError('Your device can't play HDR / 10-bit content') immediately (within ~1s) instead of entering the watchdog ladder at all. Separately, re-add a slideshow guard (sustained <~10fps over several polls => give up) so any future low-fps-but-not-frozen path can't strand the user in a permanent slideshow. Keep the relaxed 'let HW try' path only for tiers where the capability check is uncertain (the mt8695-with-more-RAM cases v3.7.9 was meant to unblock).
benchmark: Netflix/Disney+ never serve a codec/profile the device can't decode (server-side capability negotiation), so the user always gets a playable stream; when a device truly can't play something the message is instant and explicit, never a multi-second black screen — and certainly never an indefinite single-digit-fps slideshow with no error.
correction: Real symptom and correct root cause (v3.7.9 removed the fast-fail; verified at 1220-1245 — only logs HEVC_MAIN10_ATTEMPT). BUT the auditor OVER-CREDITED the friendly-error fallback. I traced the actual mt8695 path: isKnownBadMtk routes to FFmpeg software video at reset=2 (1673-1685), and HEVC IS in the AAR's enabled decoders so isFfmpegVideoAvailable('video/hevc') returns true. FFmpeg HEVC at ~3fps advances frames, so it does NOT trip the frozen-frame watchdog (which requires currentFrames == lastRenderedFrameCount) — meaning the showFriendlyError at 1628 the auditor relies on will frequently NEVER fire, and the user gets a permanent unwatchable slideshow instead of 'a delayed friendly error.' Only if FFmpeg renders ZERO frames (possible if the build's hevc config rejects 10-bit) does it freeze and error. So the real worst case is worse than the auditor stated. Also: the DeviceTier.canDecodeHevcMain10 doc comment (lines 132-134) still references a libVLC early-swap path that was DELETED in v3.7.0 — stale and misleading, but code-hygiene not customer-facing. Severity P2 holds (affects only ULTRA_LOW mt8695 + HEVC Main 10 content, a narrow slice), though the no-error slideshow variant arguably nudges toward P1 for that device class.

title: Detail→play shows a black screen + tiny bare spinner instead of the title's art during the buffer window
symptom: Customer presses Play on a movie/episode and stares at a fully black screen with a small unstyled white spinner dead-center for ~2-5s (longer on weak wifi / mt8695) until ExoPlayer renders frame 1. No poster, no backdrop, no title, no scrim. Reads as 'the app froze' rather than 'your movie is loading'.
trigger: Every VOD/Series playback start. Also every Live channel zap (tuneToChannel calls setMediaItem which clears the prior frame → STATE_BUFFERING → same bare spinner) — though Live zap additionally shows the ChannelZapOverlay with channel name, so the video area going black is slightly less disorienting there than on VOD/Series where there is literally nothing on screen.
rootCause: VERIFIED. OoustreamPlaybackFragment forces backgroundType=BG_NONE (overridden setBackgroundType at lines 85-87) and view.setBackgroundColor(TRANSPARENT) (lines 202,207), so behind the Leanback video SurfaceView there is pure black until frame 1. The only loading affordance is showBufferingOverlay(true) (line 2151) which creates a raw ProgressBar(isIndeterminate=true) with WRAP_CONTENT + Gravity.CENTER, no scrim, no background, no text (lines 2154-2161). streamIcon IS plumbed through newInstance() (line 3406/3418, restored at 3435) and IS used by the controls bar (bar.bindVod(streamName, streamIcon) line 884; bindLive line 886), but is never displayed as a full-bleed startup backdrop. There is NO onRenderedFirstFrame handler in the fragment (the only onRenderedFirstFrame override is in ExoPlayerDiagnosticListener.kt:70, which just logs — it does not fade any art).
fix: Add a full-bleed ImageView behind the Leanback video surface, load streamIcon/cover (rewriteBackdrop / PosterUrlRewriter) into it in onViewCreated with a dark gradient scrim, and keep it visible until first frame. Wire AnalyticsListener.onRenderedFirstFrame (or the existing diagnostic listener's callback) in the fragment to fade the backdrop out over ~200ms. Style showBufferingOverlay with a centered spinner over a subtle dim + optional 'Loading…' label. Reuses art the fragment already holds.
benchmark: Netflix/Disney+/Prime paint the title's key art (often the same backdrop from the detail page, shared-element) plus a branded spinner during pre-roll buffer, then crossfade to video on first frame — the customer never sees raw black between Play and picture. This bar genuinely applies to single-bitrate IPTV; it is a pure UX layer with no ABR dependency.
correction: Confirmed and correctly diagnosed. Minor correction to the trigger framing: the auditor cited line 81 as the BG_NONE source — the actual force is the setBackgroundType override at lines 85-87 plus the onViewCreated TRANSPARENT calls at 201-213. Also: on channel zap the black gap is partly softened by ChannelZapOverlay showing channel name/EPG, so 'looks like the app froze' is most acute on VOD/Series start (where the screen is truly empty) — the symptom is universal but worst on VOD/Series. Severity P1 is correct: this is the single highest-frequency perceived-quality miss (100% of watch starts) and squarely below the <3s-acceptable bar in feel even when time-to-first-frame is fine.

title: Mid-stream rebuffer flashes a bare spinner with no minimum-display threshold and no hold-last-frame treatment
symptom: During a movie/live channel, a brief network dip replaces the picture with a spinner flash, then snaps back. On a flaky pipe it strobes repeatedly. A 300-500ms refill looks like a glitch/stutter rather than a smooth recovery.
trigger: Any STATE_BUFFERING during playback: short network dips on single-bitrate IPTV, seek flushes, and the BUFFERING→READY cycling the code itself documents (buffer-storm detection). Worst in the customer-side-bottleneck scenario (pipe drains and refills repeatedly).
rootCause: VERIFIED. onPlaybackStateChanged calls showBufferingOverlay(true) immediately and synchronously on STATE_BUFFERING (line 1129) and showBufferingOverlay(false) on STATE_READY (line 1152). The overlay is a bare WRAP_CONTENT ProgressBar with no scrim (lines 2154-2161). There is no delayed/cancellable job gating the show (grep of all 6 showBufferingOverlay(true) call sites — 1100,1114,1129,1379,1580 — confirms every one is a direct synchronous call) and no minimum-visible-time once shown, so sub-second refills strobe. ExoPlayer does hold the last decoded frame on the SurfaceView during BUFFERING, but the opaque centered spinner over the otherwise-bare surface still reads as a flash.
fix: Gate showBufferingOverlay(true) behind a ~600-800ms delayed coroutine job cancelled if STATE_READY arrives first (sub-second refills never show a spinner), enforce ~500ms minimum visible once shown (can't strobe), and dim the held last frame rather than centering a stark spinner on black. Escalate to a fuller 'still buffering' treatment only after a few seconds. Leverages the last frame ExoPlayer already holds.
benchmark: Top platforms debounce the buffering indicator, hold the last frame under a subtle scrim, and surface a spinner only after the dip exceeds a grace window — transient rebuffer recoveries are perceptually invisible. This is a buffering-UX concern, not ABR, so it applies fully to single-bitrate IPTV.
correction: Confirmed. The cited existing mitigations (buffer-storm FFmpeg rebuild lines 1131-1149, stall detector, frame watchdog) are real but address decoder/codec FREEZES and reduce rebuffer FREQUENCY — they do nothing for the perceived jank of a short transient dip, exactly as the auditor states; no over-crediting here. Severity is borderline P1/P2: it does not interrupt the ability to watch (the stream recovers in <1s) so by the strict rubric it is a 'noticeable hiccup that degrades the experience' rather than a break — P1 is defensible because on a flaky connection the strobing is repeated and very visible, but a reviewer could fairly grade it P2. Keeping P1 with this caveat.

title: Empty VOD/Series category can leave fake shimmer skeletons on screen permanently (no empty-state, swap gated on non-empty)
symptom: Customer lands on a Movies/Series view whose first-loaded category resolves empty (empty server category, an over-filtered New Releases, or a fully parental-blocked category) and sees 10 shimmering placeholder posters that never resolve — looks perpetually loading with no explanation.
trigger: NARROWER than the auditor states. The skeleton→real swap is gated on isNotEmpty AND skeletonSwapped is a one-shot local var per fragment instance. So shimmer-forever only happens when the FIRST category that loads for this fragment instance resolves empty. Once ANY non-empty category has loaded, skeletonSwapped=true and the real adapter stays — a subsequently-selected empty category then shows a BLANK real grid (still bad, but not shimmering). Reachable empty-first cases: NEW_RELEASES year-filter yields nothing (VodViewModel:106-117), an else category with zero streams (line 118-121), or a category 100% parental-blocked by filterContent.
rootCause: VERIFIED. posterGrid.adapter is set to ItemBridgeAdapter(skeletonAdapter) with 10 fixed shimmer items (SeriesFragment:120-122; same in VodFragment). The swap is `if (!skeletonSwapped && movies.isNotEmpty())` (VodFragment:240) / `series.isNotEmpty()` (SeriesFragment:220). _movies/_seriesList CAN emit empty (VodViewModel:111,120 set the value to a filtered list that may be empty). VodViewModel HAS an _isLoading flag (line 31/55/67) but NEITHER fragment observes it — there is no branch distinguishing 'still loading' from 'loaded but empty', and no empty-state view or 'No titles' message (grep confirms zero empty-state strings in either fragment). PosterSkeletonPresenter has no self-timeout (no postDelayed/stopShimmer), so skeletons shimmer until the adapter is swapped.
fix: Observe _isLoading alongside the list. When the list emits empty AND loading has completed, swap the skeleton adapter out for a small friendly empty-state view ('No titles in this category') instead of leaving skeletons up. Reset the swapped/skeleton state on each selectCategory so a later empty category also shows the empty-state rather than a blank real grid.
benchmark: Streaming apps never leave skeletons up indefinitely — once a request resolves empty they show a short friendly empty-state and the loader is gone within the request window.
correction: Real, but the auditor overstated the trigger. It is NOT 'any empty category the user navigates into' — because skeletonSwapped is a one-shot per fragment instance, only the FIRST-loaded category matters for the shimmer-forever symptom; a later empty category shows a blank-but-static real grid (no shimmer). The favorites-empty fallback (v2.8.1, VodViewModel loadCategories:59-66) auto-selects the first real category, so the most common path avoids an empty default. Net: a real 'is it broken?' moment but with a narrower trigger than claimed. P2 is fair (arguably P3 given the narrow first-load-empty trigger); the auditor's 'permanent fake-loading' framing is accurate only for that first-load case.

title: Poster shimmer dismisses at 300ms keyed to image.drawable!=null, which is true the instant the synchronous color placeholder is set
symptom: On a slow connection or cold cache, the shimmer disappears after ~300ms leaving a flat dominant-color (or default dark-blue) rectangle with no artwork for another second+. The card looks 'done loading' while still blank — a subtle 'the app gave up on this poster' feel.
trigger: Scrolling VOD/Series/Home grids on slow networks or cold image cache, where the real poster bitmap takes >300ms to download after the placeholder ColorDrawable is set synchronously.
rootCause: VERIFIED. PosterPresenter starts shimmer (lines 114-116), calls ProgressiveImageLoader.loadThumbnail (line 120) which sets a ColorDrawable placeholder synchronously via Coil's placeholder() (ProgressiveImageLoader:49-53; and for null URLs setImageDrawable directly at line 40), then at 300ms checks `if (image.drawable != null)` (PosterPresenter:124) to dismiss shimmer. Because the placeholder makes image.drawable non-null almost immediately, the 300ms check passes regardless of whether the real bitmap arrived — shimmer fades over the placeholder. The 1500ms safety (lines 135-138) unconditionally kills shimmer too. Coil DOES have an onSuccess listener wired (ProgressiveImageLoader:62-75) but only for Palette extraction; it is not used to drive shimmer dismissal.
fix: Drive shimmer dismissal from Coil's actual load result, not a 300ms drawable!=null poll: add/extend an onSuccess (and onError) callback in loadThumbnail (or expose a completion lambda) and only stop/fade the shimmer when the real bitmap is set. Keep the 1500ms timeout purely as a safety net.
benchmark: Netflix/Prime keep the shimmer/placeholder running until the actual poster bitmap is decoded and presented, then crossfade — the loading affordance ends precisely when content appears, never before.
correction: Confirmed exactly as described. The crossfade(150) (ProgressiveImageLoader:54) softens the eventual placeholder→real swap, and dominant-color placeholders make the gap less ugly — but neither closes the gap that the shimmer signal ends early on slow networks. Bumped my confidence from the auditor's 'medium' to high: the synchronous-placeholder-makes-drawable-non-null mechanism is unambiguous in the code. P3 is correct (pure polish vs Netflix, cosmetic only on slow/cold-cache scrolling, no functional impact).

title: CC toggle says "CC On" even when no subtitle track exists or matches — customer enables captions, nothing ever appears
symptom: Customer presses the CC button (or KEYCODE_CAPTIONS remote key). The button turns gold and reads "CC On", a toast says "Subtitles On" — but no captions ever appear because the stream carries no embedded TEXT tracks (common for IPTV transcodes and live channels) or has subs only in a non-preferred language. The user concludes "CC is broken" and re-toggles to the same fake-positive state.
trigger: Pressing the CC fast-path button on any VOD/Series/Live stream with zero TEXT track groups, or whose only subtitle languages differ from subtitlePreferences.preferredLanguage (default 'en'). subtitlesEnabled defaults to false (SubtitlePreferences.kt:15), so the CC button IS the primary way users turn captions on — making this the dominant path, not an edge case.
rootCause: toggleClosedCaptions() (2866) computes newEnabled purely from the inverse of the current TEXT-disabled flag, then immediately calls controlsBar?.updateCcState(newEnabled) (2879) + a hardcoded "Subtitles On" toast (2881-2882). It never checks player.currentTracks for any C.TRACK_TYPE_TEXT group and never verifies post-enable that the selector actually selected a text track. setTrackTypeDisabled(TEXT,false)+setPreferredTextLanguage only express a preference — if no matching/any track exists, onCues never fires (verified: the only sv.setCues call is at 2802 inside onCues) yet the UI already committed to the gold 'On' state. The track-picker dismiss path (640-643) has the identical fake-positive: it reads only disabledTrackTypes, never whether a track is actually selected.
fix: In toggleClosedCaptions(), before enabling, check player.currentTracks.groups.any { it.type == C.TRACK_TYPE_TEXT }. If none: keep state Off + toast 'No subtitles available for this content'. If some exist, enable then hook the next onTracksChanged/onCues (or post a ~300ms delayed check): if no TEXT track ended up selected, either auto-select the first available text track regardless of language so 'On' always shows something, or revert to Off with a toast naming the available languages. Mirror the actually-selected check in the picker onTrackSelected handler (636-643) so updateCcState reflects a real selection, not just the disabled flag.
benchmark: Netflix/Disney+ only surface CC for tracks that exist and, when the profile-preferred language is absent, fall back to an available language or a clearly-labeled Off — never a silent 'On' with nothing rendering. Toggle state always reflects an actually-rendering track. This benchmark applies cleanly to IPTV (it is about track presence, not ABR).
correction: Confirmed exactly as reported. The default subtitlesEnabled=false (SubtitlePreferences.kt:15) actually STRENGTHENS this finding: the CC button is the main entry point, so the fake-positive is hit on the first thing a captions-wanting customer does. P1 severity is correct.

title: Manual non-preferred subtitle choice is dropped on next-episode autoplay; self-test stops validating after episode 1 (frozen-frame claim is wrong)
symptom: Series binge with captions ON: (b) if the user manually picked a NON-preferred-language subtitle via the track picker on the prior episode, that explicit per-track override is lost on the next episode — captions revert to the preferred language (or vanish if the next episode lacks the preferred language). (c) the subtitle pipeline self-test never re-runs for episodes 2..N, so a SUBTITLE_PIPELINE_BROKEN regression would go unlogged after the first episode (diagnostic-only, no direct customer symptom). The auditor's claimed symptom (a) — last caption frozen on screen through the whole buffering gap — does NOT occur.
trigger: Binge countdown onPlayNext (478-504) or manual skipToNextEpisode() (2332-2358), both of which reuse the SAME ExoPlayer via setMediaItem(next.url)+prepare()+play() without re-applying subtitle params or resetting subtitleSelfTestRan. Fires on every episode boundary in a binge session — but only matters when captions are ON (default OFF).
rootCause: Both next-episode paths only setMediaItem; unlike tuneToChannel (2613-2619) they do NOT reset subtitleSelfTestRan (only tuneToChannel resets it at 2603, so the self-test's `if (subtitleSelfTestRan) return` guard at 2835 blocks it for episodes 2+). For (b): the picker applies a per-track TrackSelectionOverride(group.mediaTrackGroup,...) (TrackPickerOverlay.kt:489) which references the OLD media's track group and is invalid for the new MediaItem. HOWEVER the picker ALSO calls setPreferredTextLanguage(track.language) (line 500) and saveSelectedSubtitleLanguage() persists it (2891-2904), so the chosen LANGUAGE preference does carry into the next episode via the shared trackSelector — only the exact per-track override is lost. For (a): REFUTED — decompiled Media3 1.10.0 TextRenderer.onPositionReset() and onDisabled() both call clearOutput() which emits an empty CueGroup (ImmutableList.of()) → invokeUpdateOutputInternal → output.onCues(empty) → the fragment's cueListener (2799-2811) → sv.setCues(emptyList()). So setMediaItem+prepare DOES clear the old cue within a frame; the SubtitleView does not hold a stale line through the gap.
fix: Extract reapplySubtitleState() = the 2616-2618 lines (re-enable TEXT per pref + setPreferredTextLanguage) + subtitleSelfTestRan=false, and call it from onPlayNext (490) and skipToNextEpisode (2344) right after setMediaItem. This restores per-episode self-test coverage and makes the language carry-over explicit instead of relying on the shared selector's implicit state. The frozen-cue 'setCues(emptyList()) on transition' part of the auditor's fix is unnecessary (TextRenderer already clears). For (b), if exact per-track persistence is wanted, re-resolve the override by language on the next onTracksChanged — but since the language preference already carries, this is low value.
benchmark: Netflix/Disney+ carry subtitle on/off + language selection seamlessly into the next binge episode with no caption ghosting. This app already mostly achieves that (language pref carries, TextRenderer clears stale cues); the real residual gaps are the lost exact-track override and the stopped diagnostic self-test.
correction: DOWNGRADED P1→P2 and substantially corrected. Symptom (a) 'previous episode's last caption freezes on screen until the new stream emits a cue' is REFUTED by decompiling Media3 1.10.0 TextRenderer: onPositionReset/onDisabled both call clearOutput()→onCues(empty)→sv.setCues(emptyList()), so the cue clears on transition — there is no ghost frame. Symptom (b) is real but narrower than stated: the language PREFERENCE does survive (picker sets setPreferredTextLanguage AND saveSelectedSubtitleLanguage persists it); only the exact per-track override dies. Symptom (c) self-test stopping after ep1 is CONFIRMED but is diagnostic-only with no customer-felt impact. Combined with the default subtitlesEnabled=false (only captions-ON bingers are affected) and the refuted frozen-frame, this is P2, not P1.

title: Subtitles render behind the controls bar and get dimmed/overlapped whenever controls appear
symptom: While reading captions the customer presses OK / a D-pad key and the controls bar fades in. The bottom scrim + seek bar + EPG/info row + action buttons draw on top of the subtitle text (anchored ~8% from bottom — squarely in the controls band), so the active caption is dimmed by the scrim and can be partially covered by the seek/info row for the controls' visible window. A line of dialogue is lost each time the remote is touched (worst during scrubbing, exactly when reading matters).
trigger: Any time playback controls are shown (OK press, seek/scrub, pause, channel banner) while a subtitle cue is on screen.
rootCause: configureSubtitleView adds the SubtitleView to the fragment root at 736, then the full-screen MATCH_PARENT PlayerControlsBar is addView'd at 749 AFTER it — so the controls bar is higher in z-order and paints over the SubtitleView. Verified there is no subtitleView.bringToFront()/elevation/translationZ anywhere. The fixed bottom padding screenHeight*0.08 (2794) puts captions in the controls band, and controlsManager.onVisibilityChanged (757-770) only toggles the Leanback dock's descendant focusability — it never raises the subtitle padding or brings it to front when controls show.
fix: Add the SubtitleView AFTER the controls bar (or call subtitleView.bringToFront()) so captions always draw above the scrim, AND in onVisibilityChanged raise the SubtitleView bottom padding while controls are visible (e.g. ~22% from bottom, clearing the band) and restore to 8% when controls hide, animated to match the controls fade.
benchmark: Netflix/Disney+/Prime animate subtitles upward above the transport controls the instant controls appear, so dialogue is never covered/dimmed while scrubbing. This is a generic z-order/positioning behavior, not ABR-specific — it applies to IPTV.
correction: Confirmed: view-tree order (sub at 736, bar at 749) and 8% padding (2794) verified; no bringToFront/elevation exists. Minor nuance the auditor over-stated — the controls bar is mostly transparent and the strong black caption outline (EDGE_TYPE_OUTLINE default) keeps text legible against the scrim, so it's dimming/partial-overlap rather than full occlusion. P2 is the right severity (polish gap, not a watch-breaker).

title: trimForPlayback() clears the wrong (effectively empty) Coil cache — the real display cache stays resident for the whole movie
symptom: On a long movie on a 1GB Fire TV, available heap during playback is ~14-19MB lower than the design intends because the poster bitmaps scrolled past in Home/VOD/Series grids stay resident. On worst-case content (FFmpeg software video decode, multi-MB YUV frame buffers), this is headroom that contributes to GC-pressure micro-stutters; in the tail it is an OOM-risk amplifier (not the primary cause). The customer can't attribute it to anything.
trigger: Pressing play on any VOD/Series after browsing the grids (which fill the Coil singleton cache), most acutely on mt8695/mt8167 content that escalates to the FFmpeg software video decoder mid-movie.
rootCause: Two separate Coil ImageLoaders exist. OoustreamApp implements ImageLoaderFactory.newImageLoader() (maxSizePercent(0.15), NO allowRgb565) — this is the singleton every imageView.load()/coil.load resolves to via context.imageLoader, and ALL on-screen poster/channel loading goes through ProgressiveImageLoader.loadThumbnail/loadFullRes which call imageView.load(). Separately, AdaptiveImageLoader (Hilt @Singleton, allowRgb565(true)) is provided as the injectable ImageLoader (AppModule:28) but is injected into exactly ONE consumer — PredictivePreFetcher — which never calls it (it only prefetches EPG). So AdaptiveImageLoader's cache is effectively never populated by anything. OoustreamPlaybackFragment.trimForPlayback() at line 393 clears AdaptiveImageLoader.imageLoader.memoryCache — a near-empty cache — so it is a no-op for the bitmaps that are actually resident. The real display cache (the app singleton's) is never trimmed on entering playback.
fix: Collapse to ONE ImageLoader: have OoustreamApp.newImageLoader() return adaptiveImageLoader.imageLoader (and add allowRgb565(true) — currently the survivor lacks it, doubling bitmap bytes), so imageView.load() and the injected loader are the same instance. Then make trimForPlayback() target that singleton via context.imageLoader and, instead of full clear() (which re-shimmers Home — the comment at lines 218-220 is the reason it was softened), call memoryCache.trimToSize(maxSize/4) on player entry and let it refill on exit.
benchmark: Netflix/Prime run a single tightly-budgeted image pipeline and aggressively evict browse-tier artwork when entering the player so the decoder owns the heap; they never run two competing caches and downsample (RGB565-equivalent) on constrained TV hardware. This part of the benchmark legitimately applies — it is about image-cache hygiene, not ABR.
correction: Severity corrected P1->P2 and the magnitude was inflated. (1) The cache is a HARD BYTE CEILING (maxSizePercent(0.15) of memoryClass), so on a 1GB stick (memoryClass ~96-128MB) it tops out at ~14-19MB, not 24-27MB; ARGB_8888 vs RGB565 changes how many bitmaps fit under the cap, NOT the cap itself, so 'doubling bitmap bytes' does not produce 24-27MB resident. (2) The auditor framed this purely as a no-op-trim, but the deeper truth is the AdaptiveImageLoader instance is never used at all (PredictivePreFetcher injects it and never calls it), making the RGB565 setting also dead. (3) On a 2h movie the dominant heap consumer is decoder + YUV frame buffers, not posters, so this is an OOM amplifier at the margin, not a primary cause — P2, a felt-only-on-worst-case hiccup. Still a real wiring bug worth fixing.
dimension: Memory & stability under playback (1GB Fire TV)

title: Health monitor logs heap every 60s but never acts on it — no app-level dynamic memory response during a long movie
symptom: Late in a long FFmpeg-software-decoded movie on a 1GB stick, heap pressure builds and the app takes no proactive step (no buffer tightening); in the tail risk the player dies with no warning. The only artifact is a SYSTEM/MEMORY log line read after the fact.
trigger: 90-120 minute VOD/Series on a 1GB device, especially after the watchdog has escalated to FFmpeg/platform software video decode (uncompressed frame buffers + larger decoded queue).
rootCause: PlaybackHealthMonitor's 60s memory tick (lines 103-108) computes used/total/free and calls logger.logMemory(...) — that is the entire action; there is no threshold branch that trims caches or reduces buffer targets. Confirmed via grep that NO onTrimMemory/ComponentCallbacks2/registerComponentCallbacks/onLowMemory exists anywhere in app/src, and no trimToSize call exists anywhere — so there is no app-level dynamic response. All memory defenses (largeHeap, tier buffer caps, the <=192MB low-memory load control at OoustreamPlaybackFragment:226, safeReleasePlayer) are chosen ONCE at player init.
fix: (1) In the 60s memory tick, when freeMb falls below a tier-aware threshold (e.g. used > 85% of maxMemory), trim the (unified) imageLoader.memoryCache and log a MEMORY_TRIM event. (2) The bigger lever on a single-bitrate IPTV stream is buffers: register a ComponentCallbacks2 in OoustreamApp that, when a player is foregrounded and TRIM_MEMORY_RUNNING_CRITICAL fires, nudges the load control toward smaller buffer targets. Image-cache trimming alone is low-value here since the image cache is small relative to decoder buffers.
benchmark: Netflix/YouTube TV treat onTrimMemory as a first-class signal and tighten working-set/buffering under system pressure, biasing toward holding the decoder over browse artwork. The benchmark applies for the buffer-tightening half; the image-cache half is largely already covered by Coil (see correction).
correction: Severity corrected P1->P2 and the auditor OVER-CREDITED the gap with a factual error. The claim that 'the system's own low-memory signal is ignored' is WRONG: Coil 2.x's RealImageLoader registers its OWN internal ComponentCallbacks2 and trims its memory cache automatically on TRIM_MEMORY_* — so the image cache IS shed under system pressure even without an app-level handler. The real, narrower residual gap is that there is no app-level dynamic BUFFER tightening (load control is static at init). That is real but smaller than the auditor's framing, and on a 1GB stick the existing static defenses (forLowMemory caps at <=192MB heap: VOD min/max 10s/30s; tier resolution caps; safeReleasePlayer) already bound steady-state footprint well. This is a polish/robustness gap (P2), not a P1 — there is no evidence in code or the documented customer reports of OOM-during-steady-playback once the <=192MB low-memory path is active.
dimension: Memory & stability under playback (1GB Fire TV)

title: Buffering spinner shows instantly on every dip — no grace period to hide sub-second IPTV rebuffers
symptom: During a long movie on imperfect wifi, the customer sees the loading spinner flash over the held video frame for a fraction of a second, repeatedly. The picture is fine but the flashing spinner makes it feel unstable and cheap vs Netflix, where the same dip is invisible.
trigger: Any short STATE_BUFFERING->STATE_READY round-trip — very common on single-bitrate IPTV VOD where a momentary throughput dip forces a brief refill. Fires on sub-300ms dips the user would otherwise never notice.
rootCause: onPlaybackStateChanged STATE_BUFFERING (line 1129) calls showBufferingOverlay(true) synchronously and immediately; STATE_READY (line 1152) calls showBufferingOverlay(false). showBufferingOverlay (lines 2151-2169) just flips a ProgressBar VISIBLE/GONE with no debounce. A 200ms buffering blip still toggles the spinner on then off, painting a visible flash over a held frame.
fix: Debounce the spinner: on STATE_BUFFERING post a delayed (600-800ms) showBufferingOverlay(true) stored in a Handler/Job field; on STATE_READY cancel the pending show AND hide. Dips shorter than the grace window never paint a spinner (frame just holds, like Netflix), while genuine multi-second stalls still show it. Leave the existing stall-detector/frame-watchdog timers untouched — they operate independently.
benchmark: Netflix/YouTube/Disney+ hold the last frame and reveal a loading indicator only after a sustained threshold (~0.5-1s); sub-second rebuffers are designed to be invisible. This applies to single-bitrate IPTV because it is purely a UX grace-window, not an ABR claim.
correction: Confirmed as written; severity P2 is correct. Verified the spinner is not debounced anywhere else: the stall detector (startStallDetector, line 1492) and frame watchdog are independent recovery timers and do not gate the STATE_BUFFERING->showBufferingOverlay(true) call, so they don't mitigate this. The held-last-frame behaviour the auditor credits is correct (ExoPlayer surface holds the last decoded frame on a brief rebuffer).
dimension: Memory & stability under playback (1GB Fire TV)

title: Diagnostic logger flushes to disk on every event from the player/main thread — self-amplifying jank during a degraded stretch
symptom: When a movie is already struggling (frames dropping, audio underruns, buffer churn), each event triggers a synchronous flushed disk write on the main thread, adding a few ms of main-thread I/O exactly when the device is most stressed — a small contribution to the stutter being logged.
trigger: Bursts of diagnostic events during a degraded stretch: FRAMES_DROPPED, AUDIO_UNDERRUN, AUDIO_FORMAT_CHANGED, repeated STATE_BUFFERING/READY, decoder re-inits — each routes to StreamDiagnosticLogger.write() which flush()es immediately.
rootCause: write() (line 281, @Synchronized) does writer?.write(line) then writer?.flush() on EVERY call. The log methods are invoked directly from ExoPlayer's AnalyticsListener callbacks (onDroppedVideoFrames, onAudioUnderrun, onAudioInputFormatChanged, etc.) which run on the player's application looper. The player is built (OoustreamPlaybackFragment:305-311) with NO setPlaybackLooper, so the application looper IS the main thread — every diagnostic event is a synchronous flushed file write on the UI thread, serialized via the @Synchronized monitor during a burst.
fix: Post log writes to a dedicated single-thread HandlerThread/dispatcher and replace flush-per-line with periodic flush (every 1-2s or N lines), with explicit flush in CrashLogger's uncaught-exception handler and in onPause/onDestroyView so the crash tail is still captured. Note the logger already exposes flush points (lines 238, 330) the fix can lean on.
benchmark: Production players batch diagnostics off the playback thread and flush asynchronously; crash durability is handled by flushing in the crash handler, not by flushing every routine event. Applies generally.
correction: Confirmed. Severity P3 is appropriate — the per-event main-thread flush is real and lands at the worst moment, but the magnitude is a few ms of buffered-write flush per event (BufferedWriter + small lines), and these bursts are not the typical case, so it is a polish/robustness gap, not a felt interruption on its own. The threading claim was verified: the player has no separate playback looper, so AnalyticsListener callbacks do run on main.
dimension: Memory & stability under playback (1GB Fire TV)

title: Wifi returns but player keeps spinning — fast-retry path skips the STATE_BUFFERING case
symptom: After a wifi/router blip that fully drops then restores the network connection (firing onLost→onAvailable), the picture can stay frozen with a bare spinner until the 15s (LIVE) / 30s (VOD) stall detector or 30s OkHttp readTimeout fires — even though the OS already signalled the network is back.
trigger: A wifi blip severe enough that ConnectivityManager fires onLost then onAvailable (full wifi reconnect, or default-network switch), while ExoPlayer is still sitting in STATE_BUFFERING on the old socket with playerError == null (socket not yet timed out).
rootCause: Verified: the network-return branch at line 1383 gates re-prepare on `if (p.playbackState == Player.STATE_IDLE || p.playerError != null)`. During a blip the player is STATE_BUFFERING with no error, so the branch is false and the restored-connectivity signal is ignored. The frame watchdog (line 1557) only runs in STATE_READY so it does NOT cover buffering. Recovery is left to the stall detector (STALL_TIMEOUT_LIVE_MS=15s / STALL_TIMEOUT_VOD_MS=30s, lines 3388-3389) which does p.stop()+prepare(), or the OkHttp readTimeout. Confirmed the streaming DataSource reuses the injected singleton OkHttpClient (StreamingDataFactories.buildDataSourceFactory passes it straight into OkHttpDataSource.Factory with no timeout override), so ExoPlayer streaming inherits NetworkModule's 30s connect/read/write timeouts.
fix: Broaden the network-return guard to also handle STATE_BUFFERING: `if (p.playbackState == Player.STATE_IDLE || p.playbackState == Player.STATE_BUFFERING || p.playerError != null) { retryCount = 0; p.prepare() (LIVE: p.seekToDefaultPosition() first); p.play() }`. ExoPlayer re-opens the source from the current position without clearing the held SurfaceView frame. Also lower the streaming client's connect/read timeouts (8-10s) so the error-driven path is fast when the socket truly died — but do this on a SEPARATE stream-only OkHttpClient, NOT the shared singleton (the Retrofit API path legitimately wants 30s for slow get_live_streams payloads, and the singleton is also reused by EPG/auth).
benchmark: The connectivity-callback-driven instant re-request pattern is genuinely what Netflix/YouTube TV do and it applies to single-bitrate IPTV too (re-open the HTTP byte stream from the current position). The ABR 'request the next segment' framing is IPTV-inapt, but the core idea — act on the OS connectivity signal instead of waiting on a 30s socket — is valid.
correction: Severity downgraded P0→P1. The auditor over-states this as 'the single most common scenario.' A large class of transient wifi blips keeps the SAME Network handle (device stays associated; AP momentarily drops packets) and fires NO onLost/onAvailable at all — in that case ExoPlayer auto-resumes from STATE_BUFFERING the instant bytes flow again with no prepare() needed, so the premise 'NetworkMonitor.onAvailable fired, the app already KNOWS the network is back' is FALSE and nothing is broken. The bug only bites when onLost→onAvailable actually fired AND the player hasn't yet errored to IDLE. The stall detector also backstops it at 15s/30s (annoying, not broken). Real and worth fixing, but P1 (intermittent slow reconnect), not P0 (frequently breaks watching). Also: the auditor OVER-CREDITED the existing mitigation by claiming the collector 'DOES handle the hard-disconnect-then-reconnect case' — it only does so if the player has already transitioned to STATE_IDLE/playerError by the time onAvailable fires; on a fast reconnect (blip << 30s readTimeout) the player is still STATE_BUFFERING, so even the hard-disconnect case has the same hole.

title: No WAKE_MODE_NETWORK — Fire TV radio/CPU can throttle during a stall
symptom: On a marginal connection, buffer refills/reconnects can take slightly longer and transient dips are marginally more likely to become full stalls, because the device is free to drop CPU frequency / put the wifi radio in power-save exactly while the player is trying to pull bytes to recover.
trigger: Any mid-watch buffering stall on Fire TV, especially weak wifi where the buffer drains and the player sits in STATE_BUFFERING for several seconds.
rootCause: Verified: none of the 6 ExoPlayer.Builder sites (main at 305, three rebuild factories at 1867/1987/2075, two MultiView at MultiViewPlayerManager.kt:115/452) call setWakeMode(C.WAKE_MODE_NETWORK), so ExoPlayer defaults to WAKE_MODE_NONE — no partial wake lock and no wifi lock during playback. The only awake mechanism is FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON in onIsPlayingChanged (lines 1364-1367), which addresses the display only and is actually CLEARED when isPlaying flips false — i.e. removed during a buffering stall, exactly when the radio should stay responsive. WAKE_LOCK permission IS already present in the manifest (line 20), so the fix is a one-liner with no manifest change needed.
fix: Add .setWakeMode(C.WAKE_MODE_NETWORK) to the ExoPlayer.Builder at line 305 and the three rebuild factories (and MultiView). ExoPlayer then holds a partial wake lock + WifiLock for the playback duration (acquires/releases automatically with playWhenReady), keeping the radio out of power-save during refills. WAKE_LOCK is already granted; ExoPlayer's WifiLockManager handles the wifi lock internally with no extra permission.
benchmark: WAKE_MODE_NETWORK for streamed media is recommended by the ExoPlayer integration guide and is standard for TV streaming players; it's a reliability hedge so refills aren't sabotaged by radio power-save.
correction: Severity downgraded P1→P2. The gap is real and unmitigated, but on Fire TV during ACTIVE watching the display is on and the system generally stays out of deep doze, so the customer-felt impact is 'reconnects sometimes a bit slower on marginal wifi,' not a frequent or reproducible hiccup — that's polish/reliability (P2), not a noticeable per-session degradation (P1). Still a correct best-practices fix worth landing. Auditor correctly noted the WAKE_LOCK permission is present and FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON doesn't cover the network path — both verified accurate.

title: Reconnect UX is a bare unlabeled spinner — no Reconnecting message, no offline distinction
symptom: On any stall or network drop the customer sees only a generic indeterminate spinner over the frozen frame, identical to normal buffering. No 'Reconnecting' reassurance, no offline-specific copy, until ~15-30s later a modal 'Unable to connect… try again' dialog interrupts.
trigger: Any mid-watch buffering stall or network loss. showBufferingOverlay(true) is the only in-place feedback across the normal-buffer path (line 1129), the network-loss path (line 1379), and the frame-watchdog path (line 1580).
rootCause: Verified: showBufferingOverlay (lines 2153-2163) builds a bare ProgressBar with no text label, centered over the frame, reused for normal buffer / network-loss / watchdog with no differentiated 'Reconnecting' state and no use of NetworkMonitor.isConnected to show offline copy. Confirmed no 'Reconnecting'/'Buffering'/'Waiting for network' string exists anywhere in code or strings.xml. The held-frame claim is correct: ExoPlayer never clears the SurfaceView on buffering (clearVideoSurface only runs in safeReleasePlayer) and the spinner is addView'd on top, so it's frozen-frame+spinner, not a black screen. The only network-aware messaging is the terminal modal AlertDialog (lines 2171-2197) via friendlyErrorMessage(), which appears only after retries are exhausted.
fix: Give showBufferingOverlay an optional label and show a small 'Reconnecting…' (or 'Waiting for network' when networkMonitor.state.value.isConnected == false) under the spinner on the network-loss branch (line 1379) and after the first stall-detector retry. Keep it subtle/non-modal over the held frame; reserve the AlertDialog for true last resort. The connectivity signal to distinguish offline vs buffering is already in hand.
benchmark: Netflix/YouTube TV show a quiet labeled retry indicator over the paused frame and resume silently when bytes return, clearly signalling offline vs ordinary buffering without a modal — apt and applicable here.
correction: Severity downgraded P1→P2. Genuine polish gap vs Netflix and all code claims verified, but it does not interrupt or degrade the actual playback — the picture is held and recovery still happens; this is purely a reassurance/affordance gap on the 10-foot UI. That's P2 friction, not a P1 experience degradation. Auditor's held-frame credit and friendlyErrorMessage observation are both accurate.

title: Stall recovery does stop()+fixed delay instead of an in-place refill
symptom: A brief throughput dip that could recover invisibly instead, once the stall timer trips, tears the stream down (p.stop()) and waits a fixed delay (first hit 1s) before prepare()+play() — adding avoidable downtime on a connection that was merely slow, not dead.
trigger: A transient bandwidth dip on a single-bitrate IPTV stream where the buffer drains but the connection is alive; player enters STATE_BUFFERING and the stall detector fires after STALL_TIMEOUT (15s LIVE / 30s VOD).
rootCause: Verified: the stall detector at line 1505-1508 calls p.stop() then delay(delayMs) (RETRY_DELAYS_MS[0]=1000 on the first escalation, up to 15000) BEFORE p.prepare()+p.play(). A bare prepare() (no stop, shorter/no delay) would reconnect faster on a still-alive socket. The fixed buffer cushions (LIVE 5s min / VOD 15s min in BufferConfigs.forContentType) don't grow after a recent stall, so a thin pipe keeps buffer-drain-rebuffering. Confirmed the MediaItem retains its position across stop()/prepare(), so VOD recovery resumes from the stalled spot (no replay-from-start) — this is purely a latency concern, not a resume-loss bug.
fix: For the first stall escalation, prefer an in-place refill: skip stop() and call p.prepare() with no (or a much shorter) fixed delay; reserve hard stop()+escalating delay for repeated failures. Optionally grow minBufferMs after a recent stall.
benchmark: PARTIALLY APT. The 'in-place prepare instead of stop+wait' half is valid and IPTV-applicable. But the 'deep adaptive pre-buffer absorbs the dip invisibly' half is an ABR/single-bitrate mismatch: per the triage rules, IPTV is single-bitrate with no lower rung, and the documented real customer pattern is a SUSTAINED customer-side bottleneck (consistent 13-15s refills) where no pre-buffer depth helps — buffer→drain→rebuffer is inevitable. A deeper post-stall pre-buffer only helps genuine momentary dips, not the common sustained-throttle case.
correction: Severity downgraded P2→P3. The in-place-refill optimization is legitimate but only saves a 1s fixed delay on the FIRST escalation, and only fires after the stream has already been stalled for the full 15s/30s stall window — by which point the customer has long seen a spinner regardless, so shaving the recovery delay is a marginal polish win. The escalating retry ladder already recovers and STATE_READY resets retryCount. Auditor's medium confidence is appropriate; I'm pushing it to P3 because the felt benefit is small and the 'deep adaptive pre-buffer' benchmark half doesn't apply to the dominant single-bitrate sustained-bottleneck scenario.

title: Every play action opens on a black screen + bare spinner (no poster/backdrop/last-frame hold)
symptom: Press Play (or zap a channel) and the screen goes fully black with a small centered spinner for the entire TTFF window (2-5s on a 1GB Fire TV over IPTV). It reads as 'the app froze' or 'the stream is broken' rather than 'loading'.
trigger: Any transition into the player: hero Play, search result, Continue Watching, deep-link, and every live zap. Fires on 100% of plays.
rootCause: Verified: showBufferingOverlay() (line 2151) lazily creates a single indeterminate ProgressBar, WRAP_CONTENT, Gravity.CENTER, and addView()s it over a BG_NONE VideoSupportFragment SurfaceView that is black until first frame (setBackgroundType forces BG_NONE, line 85-87). There is no ImageView, no backdrop, no poster, no dim scrim — grep for ImageView/Coil/backdrop/load() in the fragment returns nothing for a loading screen. streamIcon IS passed into newInstance and stored (line 3435) but is consumed only by the controls bar bindVod (line 884), never loaded as a full-screen loading background. The overlay is hidden only on STATE_READY (line 1152) — there is NO onRenderedFirstFrame handler anywhere in the fragment, so there is no cross-fade-from-art into the picture.
fix: Add a full-screen ImageView behind the SurfaceView; Coil-load the passed streamIcon (and, for VOD, the cover) into it in onViewCreated; show it with a dim scrim whenever STATE_BUFFERING and no first frame has rendered; register an onRenderedFirstFrame (Player.Listener) callback to cross-fade it out. Replace the centered ProgressBar with art + a slim bottom shimmer. For zap, don't clear the outgoing frame until the new first frame renders.
benchmark: Netflix/Disney+/YouTube TV hold the selected title's art or a full-bleed backdrop with a subtle loading shimmer during TTFF and cross-fade straight into the picture — the user never sees black, so a 2-3s start feels near-instant. This benchmark DOES apply to single-bitrate IPTV: it's a perceptual-UX fix, not an ABR fix.

title: Channel zap drops to black + spinner instead of holding the last frame; banner lags 500ms
symptom: Changing channels flashes black + spinner for ~1-3s before the new channel appears (plus a 500ms-late channel banner), instead of a clean cut. Channel surfing feels sluggish and 'broken' between channels.
trigger: Every live channel change via the zap overlay or up/down channel keys.
rootCause: Verified: tuneToChannel mutes (line 2631) then calls setMediaItem/prepare/play (lines 2633-2635) on the same ExoPlayer; the new prepare blanks the surface and STATE_BUFFERING paints the bare spinner over black (same root cause as black-spinner-no-art). The channel banner is posted behind a 500ms delay (line 2649-2651) instead of synchronously on key-press. No last-frame hold and no decoded pre-warm of the adjacent channel (predictive pre-fetch is metadata-only).
fix: Show the channel banner + target-channel logo/art synchronously on key-press; keep the outgoing frame (or a dim channel-art scrim) visible during the buffer instead of black; consider a small next/prev pre-warm for up/down surfing. Shares the art-overlay infrastructure with black-spinner-no-art.
benchmark: YouTube TV / cable-style TV apps target sub-1.5s zaps and mask the buffer by holding the old frame or showing channel art + banner immediately, so the change feels like a clean cut. Applies to IPTV (perceptual, not ABR).
correction: Same underlying defect as black-spinner-no-art (bare spinner overlay + no first-frame/last-frame logic) specialized to zap; the 500ms-late banner is an additional verified contributor. P2 is appropriate — channel surfing is a frequent live-TV interaction but each individual zap still recovers.

title: Search movies silently jump to the middle (no Resume dialog), unlike every other surface
symptom: Searching a partly-watched movie and pressing it drops the customer straight into the middle with no choice — yet the SAME movie from Home, the detail page, or Continue Watching asks 'Resume or Start Over?'. The inconsistency is surprising and can strand them deep in a film they wanted to restart.
trigger: Playing a VOD result directly from the Search screen when watch progress exists.
rootCause: Verified: SearchFragment.navigateToContent's VOD branch (line 611-628) builds newInstance WITHOUT forceStartFromBeginning and WITHOUT routing through ResumePlaybackHelper. In the player, needsResume = contentType != LIVE && !hasResumed && !forceBeginningArg (line 411) is therefore true, so getResumePositionSync() auto-seeks to the saved offset (lines 417-423) with no prompt. Home (playVodWithResumeCheck, HomeFragment 1876), VodDetail (124-146), and SeriesDetail all gate through ResumePlaybackHelper.showIfNeeded, so they prompt. The two paths genuinely disagree.
fix: Route SearchFragment.navigateToContent's VOD branch through a resume-check (ResumePlaybackHelper.showIfNeeded with a local getWatchProgress query) so resume behavior is identical everywhere.
benchmark: Netflix/Disney+ behave identically from every entry point (search, row, detail) — same resume/start-over affordance, no surface-dependent surprises.
correction: Confirmed exactly as reported. Note this is partly a sub-case of the broader resume-modal-friction debate: if the app moved to 'auto-resume + in-player Restart chip' (the benchmark), Search's silent resume would actually be the CORRECT behavior and the other surfaces' modals would be the inconsistency. Either way the surfaces must converge. P2 is fair (low frequency: needs a searched, partly-watched title).

title: Resume requires a blocking modal choice instead of just continuing
symptom: Pressing Play / 'Resume from 1:12:03' on a partly-watched movie pops a blocking AlertDialog the customer must answer before anything plays — an extra D-pad press on the most common action (continuing what you were watching), redundant when the button already said 'Resume from X'.
trigger: Playing any VOD/series with >5% saved progress from Home, VOD detail, or series detail (Continue Watching already resumes without a dialog).
rootCause: Verified: ResumePlaybackHelper.showIfNeeded always throws an AlertDialog when progress > 5% and not completed (lines 17-29). VodDetail's button is already labeled 'Resume from X' (line 277) yet still triggers the same modal (line 128). Continue Watching (navigateToContinueWatching) correctly resumes directly with no prompt.
fix: When the affordance already says 'Resume', resume directly and surface a quiet 'Start Over'/'Restart' chip in the player controls (or a brief snackbar with an undo action) instead of a blocking pre-play dialog. Reserve the modal for genuinely ambiguous entry points.
benchmark: Netflix/YouTube TV auto-resume on Play and expose 'Restart'/'Watch from start' as a secondary in-player control — no blocking pre-roll dialog.
correction: Real and correctly P3 (a polish/UX-opinion gap, not a defect — the modal is fully functional and shows the exact resume timestamp). This is a design-philosophy call; some users prefer the explicit prompt. Keeping P3.

title: Live deep-link shows placeholder 'Channel 1234' name and seeds no channel list
symptom: Opening a live channel via an ooustream:// deep link shows the title 'Channel 481516' in the banner instead of the real channel name, and D-pad channel up/down/zap does nothing afterward because no channel list was seeded.
trigger: Following an ooustream:// live deep link.
rootCause: PARTIAL. Verified TRUE: MainActivity deep-link Live branch builds a REAL URL via contentRepository.buildLiveStreamUrl(streamId) (line 383) but hardcodes streamName = 'Channel ${target.streamId}' (line 388) with no channel lookup, and never calls setChannels — so the player has no channel list and zap/up-down is dead. Verified FALSE for the auditor's headline claim: the 'For You Live' recommendation does NOT pass an empty URL. That row's clicks go through HomeFragment.navigateToLiveChannel (line 1346), which builds a real URL via buildLiveStreamUrl(channel.channelId) AND seeds the full channel list (lines 1351-1359). The empty-URL 'live' branch in navigateToRecommendation (line 1842-1849, streamUrl="") is DEAD CODE: RecommendationEngine only ever emits type="vod" or type="series" (RecommendationEngine.kt: all 5 RecommendedItem constructions are vod/series, never "live"), and HomeViewModel never constructs a live RecommendedItem. So no customer can reach the empty-URL path.
fix: Deep-link Live branch: look up the channel by streamId to pass the real name and seed the channel list (setChannels) so zap works; fall back to a generic name only if lookup fails. Optionally delete the unreachable empty-URL 'live' branch in navigateToRecommendation to prevent a future regression.
benchmark: Live TV apps (YouTube TV) never open a player without a resolvable stream and always show the real channel/program name on tune-in, with channel up/down working immediately.
correction: Auditor MIS-attributed and over-severitied. The 'empty URL -> instant error/black screen' half is FALSE (unreachable dead code; the real For You Live path builds a valid URL and seeds channels). Only the deep-link placeholder NAME is real, plus a MISSED real consequence the auditor didn't state: the deep-link path also seeds no channel list, so zap is silently dead after a deep-link tune-in. Deep links are a rare entry point and a wrong banner name doesn't break watching, so this drops from P2 to P3.

title: Movies route through a detail screen before Play (extra step), but Play itself is NOT network-gated
symptom: Picking a movie from a VOD/Series grid tile or the hero 'More Info' opens a separate detail screen rather than playing directly — an extra full-screen navigation versus a streaming app where the tile plays. A late focus jump can also occur when metadata returns.
trigger: Browsing movies via grids or hero 'More Info'; tapping a series in search.
rootCause: PARTIAL. Verified TRUE: the default grid-tile and hero 'More Info' action routes to VodDetailFragment (an extra screen) rather than playing directly; the hero primary button has a direct play path but tiles don't. Verified FALSE / over-stated by the auditor: Play is NOT gated on the get_vod_info network call. The play URL is built from containerExtension, which is ALREADY passed in from the grid payload (VodFragment.kt line 99 -> VodDetailFragment ARG_CONTAINER_EXT, used at line 126 with ?: 'mp4' fallback); the 'Resume from X' label comes from viewModel.watchProgress, a LOCAL Room Flow (line 268), not the network. So a customer CAN press Resume/Play immediately on placeholders. The only genuine network-coupled jank is line 260: when loadVodInfo returns, playButton.requestFocus() fires again and can yank focus back if the user had D-padded away to read the plot.
fix: Make the grid-tile primary action play directly (with a resume check) and reserve detail for long-press/'More Info'. Remove the redundant post-API playButton.requestFocus() (line 260) so returning metadata doesn't steal focus. The containerExtension pre-warm the auditor recommends is already done.
benchmark: Netflix/Prime: clicking a tile plays immediately (resume or start) with a single big Play; details are secondary.
correction: Auditor over-credited the network dependency. The claimed 'metadata API call must return before Play is usable' is FALSE: extension is pre-warmed from the grid payload and the resume label is local-DB-driven. The real residue is (1) one extra navigation step (a legitimate but minor flow choice — many streaming apps DO show a detail page for movies) and (2) a post-API focus-steal at line 260. Drops from P2 to P3.
